cultivates.why: every part of the act is seen as the one reality
the meal or the work becomes an offering

commentary.reading: Shankara: for the knower every element of the sacrifice is nothing but Brahman, so his action is in truth no action; the verse is traditionally recited before meals.

claim: Even the most sinful of all sinners crosses all wrongdoing by the raft of knowledge alone.

heals.why: no past is too heavy for understanding to carry a person across
'even if you were the worst of all' leaves no one outside

cultivates.why: trust that knowledge frees from what was done

needs: the reader's burden is guilt for something they did; it says nothing about being loved or unloved

commentary.reading: Shankara: even if you were the worst of sinners, with the raft of knowledge of Brahman you will cross the whole ocean of sin; for the seeker of liberation even merit counts as sin here.

claim: The ignorant, faithless, doubting person perishes; for the doubter there is neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.
needs: doubt here is refusal to trust teacher and teaching at all, not honest questioning or an anxious mind

commentary.reading: Shankara: the ignorant and the faithless perish, but the doubting mind is the worst of the three, for it gains neither this world, nor the next, nor happiness.

line_issue: The line softens 'perishes' but is still a verdict, and the app tags it for overthinking. Keep it for a faith context only. Corrected: 'The one who neither knows nor trusts, and doubts everything, is lost. For the doubting mind there is no happiness in this world or the next.'

claim: Cutting the heart's ignorance-born doubt with the sword of knowledge, one should take to yoga and stand up.

heals.why: doubt is named as born of not knowing, and is to be cut by understanding, then acted past

cultivates.why: 'stand up': the chapter ends on rising
knowledge as the blade

needs: the reader has done the thinking and is stuck at the edge of acting

commentary.reading: Shankara: with the sword of knowledge of the self cut the doubt lodged in your intellect, born of non-discrimination, resort to karma yoga and arise.

claim: For protecting the good, destroying evildoers and establishing dharma, the Lord takes birth age after age.

heals.why: protection of the good and an end to wrongdoing are named as God's own purpose
the good are not left unprotected

cultivates.why: trust that right is restored
the good have a protector

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: for protecting those on the right path, destroying doers of evil and firmly setting up dharma, he comes into being in every age.

claim: The yogi giving up the fruit of action attains abiding peace; the non-yogi, attached to fruit through desire, is bound.

heals.why: the binding is traced to the clinging, not to the work
chasing the payoff is what chains

cultivates.why: lasting peace follows giving up the fruit

commentary.reading: Shankara: the one who acts for the Lord and gives up the fruit gains the peace that comes of steadfastness, by stages; the other, driven by desire, is bound.

claim: The wise see the same in a learned, humble brahmin, a cow, an elephant, a dog and an outcaste.

heals.why: rank and learning do not change what a being is
the scale that comparison uses is set aside

cultivates.why: equal vision across every rank
the same Brahman in all bodies

commentary.reading: Shankara: the wise see the one changeless Brahman alike in the highest, the middling and the lowest, untouched by their qualities.

claim: The knower of Brahman, steady and undeluded, abiding in Brahman, neither rejoices at the pleasant nor is agitated by the unpleasant.

cultivates.why: neither carried away nor crushed
a steady understanding
the evenness rests on abiding in Brahman

needs: not a reply to fresh grief or injury

commentary.reading: Shankara: only those who take the body as the self are elated and dejected by the pleasant and unpleasant; the knower of Brahman, who sees the one faultless self, is not.

line_issue: The line drops the ground the verse gives for the steadiness. Corrected: 'The one who knows Brahman and rests there, steady and clear, is not carried away by the pleasant or shaken by the unpleasant.'

claim: One unattached to outer contacts finds the happiness in the self; joined to Brahman, he enjoys undying happiness.

heals.why: when outer things stop satisfying, the verse points to a happiness that was never outside
the search turns inward

cultivates.why: a happiness within that does not run out
joy belongs to the self
unhooked from outer contacts

commentary.reading: Shankara: with mind unattached to outer sense contacts, he finds the joy that is in the inner self, and absorbed in Brahman attains imperishable happiness.

claim: Knowing Krishna as enjoyer of sacrifices, great Lord of all worlds and friend of all beings, one attains peace.

heals.why: the Lord of all the worlds is named as the friend of every being, the reader included
the one who rules everything wishes you well

cultivates.why: peace comes from knowing him so
trust in a well-wisher who asks nothing back

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: suhrid is one who does good without expecting any return; knowing the Lord as that friend dwelling in the heart of all, one attains peace.

claim: One who neither hates nor desires is a constant renouncer; free of the pairs, he is easily released from bondage.

heals.why: renunciation is redefined as dropping resentment
and dropping craving, wherever one lives

cultivates.why: an inner letting go that needs no change of address
free of the pairs of opposites

commentary.reading: Shankara: the karma yogi who neither hates pain nor longs for pleasure is to be known as always a renouncer, even while acting.

claim: One who does due work without depending on its fruit is the renouncer and yogi, not the fireless or inactive.

heals.why: quitting is not the mark of freedom; doing what is needed without leaning on the reward is

cultivates.why: not depending on the fruit
staying with the work that ought to be done

commentary.reading: Shankara: this praises the karma yogi who gives up the fruit: he too is a renouncer and yogi in a secondary sense, not only the one who has given up the ritual fire and action.

claim: Having gained that, one counts no other gain greater; established in it, one is not shaken even by heavy sorrow.

heals.why: there is a footing that even heavy sorrow does not move
a gain that cannot be lost

cultivates.why: unshaken by great grief
'that' is the self found in meditation (6.20-21)
no gain beyond it is wanted

needs: the passage 6.20-21 names what is gained; alone the line promises immunity to sorrow and can read as a reproach to someone grieving

commentary.reading: Shankara: having gained the self, one thinks no other gain higher; established in the truth of the self, one is not moved even by great pain such as a sword stroke.

claim: Yoga is disconnection from union with sorrow; it should be practised with determination and an undespairing mind.

heals.why: the practice is to be kept up with a heart that refuses to despair
'anirvinna': do not let weariness with the effort set in

cultivates.why: practise with determination
keeping on without losing heart

commentary.reading: Shankara: yoga is so called by contrary usage, being separation from contact with pain; practise it with conviction and a mind free of dejection.

claim: Little by little one should withdraw, with intellect held by steadiness; fixing the mind in the self, think of nothing.

heals.why: the mind is settled little by little, not all at once
a sitting practice of resting the mind and letting other thoughts go

cultivates.why: understanding held by steadiness
the mind resting in the self

commentary.reading: Shankara: withdraw gradually, not abruptly, with the intellect held by firmness; make the mind abide in the self, thinking 'the self alone is all'; this is the highest rule of yoga.

claim: One who sees Krishna everywhere and everything in him is never lost to Krishna, nor Krishna to him.

heals.why: 'I am never lost to him, and he is never lost to me': the bond cannot be broken by distance
nothing seen in him is ever fully gone

cultivates.why: seeing him in everything
the one self in all and all in it
never lost

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: for one who sees the Lord, the self of all, in all beings, the Lord never goes out of sight, nor he out of the Lord's, since his self and the Lord's are one. Ramanuja: the Lord never withdraws his regard from such a one.

claim: Yoga is hard to attain for the uncontrolled, but attainable through right means by the self-controlled who strive.

heals.why: hard, yes, and within reach with effort and the right means

cultivates.why: striving is named as what makes it possible
self-mastery through practice

commentary.reading: Shankara: for one whose mind is not mastered by practice and dispassion yoga is hard to gain; for one who has mastered it and strives by the means stated, it can be gained.

claim: Arjuna asks what end awaits one with faith who strives too little, strays from yoga and misses its perfection.

depicts.why: the fear of having believed, tried, slipped and not made it
'what becomes of such a person?'

commentary.reading: Plain sense, as in Shankara: Arjuna asks about one who has faith but whose effort slackens and whose mind strays from yoga at the end.

claim: Arjuna asks whether one fallen from both paths perishes like a torn cloud, unsupported and bewildered.

depicts.why: afraid of ending up with neither the old life nor the new
'like a torn cloud, with nowhere to stand'

commentary.reading: Shankara: fallen from both the path of action and the path of yoga, does he perish like a cloud torn from one mass and not joined to another?

claim: One who is even-minded toward well-wishers, friends, enemies, neutrals, the hateful, kin, the good and sinners excels.

cultivates.why: an even mind toward friend, foe, stranger, saint and wrongdoer

needs: a seeker's ideal; told to someone being mistreated it asks them to feel the same toward the one harming them

commentary.reading: Shankara: the one who does not judge 'who is this, what has he done' toward any of these, good or sinful, is the best among those established in yoga.

claim: Krishna is the strength of the strong free of desire and passion, and in beings the desire not opposed to dharma.

heals.why: wanting is not condemned as such; desire in line with what is right is called divine

cultivates.why: strength without grasping is named as God's presence in the strong
the line between desire that accords with dharma and desire that does not

commentary.reading: Shankara: kama is thirst for what is not had and raga is attachment to what is had; strength free of both, needed only to keep the body, is the Lord; so is desire not against scripture, such as for food and drink.

claim: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Krishna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth and the wise.

heals.why: turning to God only because one is in trouble is counted as good, not as lesser
those who come out of need are called virtuous too

cultivates.why: every reason for turning is honoured
the distressed are named first among those who come

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: all four are people of good deeds; 7.17-18 add that the wise one is dearest, though all are noble. The line's 'all four are welcome' is fair to 7.18's 'all these are noble'.

claim: Whatever state one remembers when leaving the body at the end, that one attains, being always absorbed in it.

cultivates.why: what the mind dwells on through life is what it holds at the end

needs: a reader thinking about how to live toward death; never someone with a dying relative

commentary.reading: Shankara: whatever being one thinks of at the time of death one attains, because of lifelong dwelling on it; hence the instruction in 8.7 to remember the Lord always.

line_issue: The line hides that the verse is about the moment of death. Corrected: 'Whatever a person holds in mind when leaving the body at the end, to that they go, for it is what they dwelt on all along.'

claim: Therefore one should remember Krishna at all times and fight; with mind and intellect offered to him, one surely reaches him.

heals.why: remembrance runs alongside the work, so the work is not carried alone

cultivates.why: mind and understanding given to him
'you will come to me, without doubt'

needs: a devotional reader

commentary.reading: Shankara: remember the Lord at all times as scripture teaches and do your own duty of battle; with mind and intellect fixed on him you will reach him.

claim: Whatever one does, eats, offers, gives or practises as austerity should be done as an offering to Krishna.

heals.why: ordinary acts, even eating, are given a direction

cultivates.why: everything done becomes an offering to him
each meal and gift is handed back
work as offering

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: whatever you do of your own accord, whatever you eat, sacrifice, give or practise as austerity, do it as an offering to the Lord; 9.28 gives the fruit: freedom from the bonds of action.

line_issue: 'Endure' misrenders tapasyasi and the one offered to is dropped. Corrected: 'Whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you give, whatever discipline you keep, do it as an offering to me.'

claim: Krishna is the same to all, none hated or dear; yet his devotees are in him and he in them.

heals.why: no one is disfavoured by God
'they are in me and I am in them'
no one is hated by him

cultivates.why: devotion is what brings the closeness
his evenness toward all

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: he is like fire, which warms those who come near and not those far off, without partiality; those who worship him abide in him by their own nature, and he in them.

claim: Even one of very bad conduct who worships Krishna with undivided devotion is to be deemed good, having resolved rightly.

heals.why: the past conduct does not fix the verdict; the turning does
'he is to be counted among the good'

cultivates.why: right resolve is what is honoured
undivided turning to him

needs: a reader open to God who carries guilt for their own conduct

commentary.reading: Shankara: even one of very evil conduct who worships the Lord with undivided mind must be considered good, because his resolve is right. Ramanuja likewise stresses the rightness of the resolve.

claim: Such a one quickly becomes righteous and attains lasting peace; Krishna's devotee never perishes.

heals.why: change comes soon after the turning
'my devotee is never lost', given as a vow to be proclaimed

cultivates.why: a promise to hold to
lasting peace is promised
never lost

needs: follows 9.30; a devotional reader

commentary.reading: Shankara: giving up bad conduct he soon becomes righteous in mind and gains lasting peace; Arjuna is told to proclaim firmly that the Lord's devotee does not perish.

claim: Krishna is the self seated in the hearts of all beings, and their beginning, middle and end.

heals.why: God is not elsewhere; he is the self in one's own heart

cultivates.why: the Lord is the inmost self of every being
he holds the beginning, middle and end

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: the Lord is the inner self to be meditated on always, dwelling in the heart of all beings; one unable to do that may meditate on him in the glories that follow.

claim: With minds and lives given to Krishna, enlightening one another and always speaking of him, his devotees are content and delight.

depicts.why: devotees pictured delighting together in talk of him

heals.why: company gathered around a shared love is shown as a source of joy

cultivates.why: they are content
they delight
mind and life given to him

needs: a devotional reader

commentary.reading: Shankara: with minds on the Lord and lives given to him, teaching one another and speaking of him, they find contentment and delight as if meeting a beloved.

claim: Seeing the blazing, sky-touching, open-mouthed form, Arjuna trembles within and finds neither steadiness nor peace.

depicts.why: 'my inmost self trembles'
'I find no steadiness and no calm'

needs: the scene of the cosmic form; the fear is awe before God's terrible aspect

commentary.reading: Plain sense: before the terrible cosmic form Arjuna's inner self is shaken and he finds neither firmness nor peace.

line_issue: The line cuts the vision and keeps only the reaction, which is acceptable as a hook but should name what is seen. Corrected: 'Seeing you fill the sky, blazing, my heart trembles within me and I can find neither steadiness nor calm.'

claim: Thrilled at seeing the unseen yet shaken with fear, Arjuna asks the Lord to show his familiar form and be gracious.

depicts.why: 'my mind is shaken with fear' even while thrilled
he asks for grace and the familiar face

needs: the scene of the cosmic form

commentary.reading: Plain sense: glad at seeing what was never seen, and afraid, Arjuna asks to see the earlier gentle form.

claim: Krishna tells Arjuna not to be afraid or bewildered at the terrible form, and to see his familiar form again, fear gone.

heals.why: inside the scene, the one who frightened him is the one who comforts him and returns to a gentle form

cultivates.why: 'free from fear and glad at heart'

needs: the scene: God withdrawing a terrifying vision; alone it just tells a frightened person not to be afraid

commentary.reading: Plain sense: the Lord comforts Arjuna and shows again the gentle form; 11.50 says he consoled the frightened one.

claim: Those who restrain the senses, are even-minded everywhere and delight in the welfare of all beings also reach Krishna.

cultivates.why: delighting in the good of all beings
even-minded everywhere

needs: completes 12.3 on those who worship the formless

commentary.reading: Shankara: those who meditate on the imperishable, with senses restrained and equal vision, intent on the good of all, reach the Lord; 12.5 adds that their path is harder for the embodied.

claim: Some see the self in themselves by meditation, others by the yoga of knowledge, and others by the yoga of action.

heals.why: there is more than one valid way; one's own temperament has a path

cultivates.why: each route is affirmed as reaching the self
invites finding the way that fits

commentary.reading: Shankara: the best see by meditation, the middling by discriminating knowledge of the gunas and the self, others by action offered to the Lord, which leads to knowledge through purity of mind.

claim: Others who do not know these ways worship as they have heard from others; they too cross beyond death, devoted to hearing.

heals.why: the one who can only listen and trust is not left out

cultivates.why: devotion to what one has heard from teachers is itself enough to cross

commentary.reading: Shankara: others, unable to know by any of these means, hear from teachers and worship with faith; even they cross over death, so how much more those who can discriminate.

claim: As all-pervading space is not tainted because of its subtlety, the self present in every body is not tainted.

heals.why: what you are at root is not stained by what the body has done or undergone
no criticism reaches that in you which is like the sky

cultivates.why: the self is like space: in everything, marked by nothing
nothing can stain it

needs: week three; a reader already introduced to the self as distinct from body and mind

commentary.reading: Shankara: as space, though everywhere, is not touched by what it contains because it is subtle, so the self, though in every body, is not touched by the body's actions and their fruits.

claim: Darkness, inactivity, heedlessness and delusion arise when tamas predominates.

heals.why: the heaviness is named as a rise of tamas, a passing quality of nature, and not as the person
drift and carelessness are read as signs, not as character

cultivates.why: reading one's state by its signs

commentary.reading: Shankara: aprakasha is lack of discrimination, apravritti its effect, lack of effort; heedlessness and delusion follow. These are the signs that tamas has risen.

claim: Seated like one unconcerned, unshaken by the gunas, knowing that only the gunas act, he stays firm and does not waver.

heals.why: the churn is the gunas moving; one can sit as its witness
thoughts are watched as nature acting, not obeyed

cultivates.why: you are the one who watches the qualities move
unshaken by whichever state is passing
sitting like one with no stake

commentary.reading: Shankara: the knower sits like a neutral party, not moved from his own nature by the gunas, knowing 'the gunas, turned into body, senses and objects, act on one another'.

line_issue: 'Just moods' shrinks the gunas. Corrected: 'Sitting like a witness, unshaken, knowing that it is only the qualities of nature at work, such a person stays steady.'

claim: Tamas, born of ignorance, deludes all embodied beings and binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep.

heals.why: laziness and oversleep are explained as the binding of tamas, common to all embodied beings
heedlessness is named as how dullness holds on

cultivates.why: knowing what is holding one down

commentary.reading: Shankara: tamas, born of ignorance, deludes all the embodied and binds through heedlessness, sloth and sleep.

claim: Krishna is seated in every heart; from him come memory, knowledge and their loss; all the Vedas make him known.

heals.why: he is seated in one's own heart
even forgetting comes from him, so a lapse of clarity is not only one's own failure

cultivates.why: the one the Vedas speak of is the one within
memory and understanding are his gifts

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: The Lord dwells as the self in the hearts of all; memory and knowledge, and their loss, come from him according to beings' deeds.

claim: Free of pride and delusion, attachment conquered, ever in the self, desires gone, freed from the pairs, the undeluded reach the imperishable.

heals.why: pride is the first thing dropped
the fault of attachment is conquered

cultivates.why: always dwelling on the self
desires turned away

needs: a seeker's horizon

commentary.reading: These are the qualities of those who, having taken refuge in the primal Person, reach the unchanging goal: free of pride and delusion, devoted to contemplating the self, desires wholly gone.

line_issue: The line keeps two of six marks and loses 'ever dwelling in the self'. Corrected: 'Free of pride and delusion, attachment overcome, always resting in the self, desires stilled, released from the pull of pleasure and pain, the clear-sighted reach what does not fade.'

claim: An eternal portion of Krishna becomes the living soul in the world and draws the mind and five senses abiding in nature.

heals.why: what you are is an eternal part of God; smallness is not the truth of you
no act removes that belonging
the soul is his own portion, never cut off

cultivates.why: the living self is an eternal part of the Lord
worth that rests on what one is

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: 'part' is figurative, like the space in a jar being a part of space; the soul is the Lord himself seen through a limiting adjunct. Ramanuja takes the soul as a real and eternal part, a mode of the Lord.

claim: The demonic, deluded by ignorance, say: I am rich and well-born, who equals me; I will sacrifice, give and rejoice.

depicts.why: the inner speech of someone drunk on wealth and standing, quoted directly
'who else is equal to me?'

needs: a reader examining their own pride; the speaker is describing the demonic nature

commentary.reading: Those of demonic nature think: I am wealthy and of high birth, none is my equal; even their giving and sacrifice are for self-display.

claim: Self-conceited, stubborn, drunk with wealth and honour, the demonic perform sacrifices in name only, with hypocrisy and against rule.

cultivates.why: giving or worship done for display is named as empty

needs: describes the demonic nature; a mirror only for one examining pride

commentary.reading: Esteemed only by themselves, unbending, intoxicated by wealth and honour, they perform sacrifices in name only, for show and without regard to the rule.

claim: One released from these three gates of darkness does what is good for the self and reaches the highest goal.

heals.why: freedom from desire, anger and greed is shown as the opening to one's own good

cultivates.why: acting for one's real good once the three are set down

needs: follows 16.21, which names the three gates

commentary.reading: Freed from desire, anger and greed, the gates to the darkness of hell, a person practises what is good for the self and so reaches liberation.

claim: The divine nature leads to liberation and the demonic to bondage; Arjuna need not grieve, being born to the divine.

heals.why: after a list of faults, the teacher says: this is not you; you were born to the good
a direct assurance of worth from the teacher
the fear of being one of the lost is answered

cultivates.why: you are born to the divine endowment
trust in one's own good nature

commentary.reading: Seeing Arjuna wonder which nature is his, the Lord says: do not grieve, you are born for the divine endowment.

line_issue: 'Don't worry' flattens 'do not grieve', and 'harsh ones' misnames the demonic nature. Corrected: 'The divine qualities lead to freedom and the demonic to bondage. Do not grieve; you were born to the divine.'

claim: Austerity done from foolish obstinacy, with self-torture, or to ruin another, is called tamasic.

heals.why: discipline that works by tormenting oneself is named as the dark kind, not the admirable kind
self-punishment is not counted as virtue

cultivates.why: telling discipline from self-harm
toward oneself: torment is not required

commentary.reading: Austerity undertaken with a deluded notion, by torturing oneself, or to destroy another, is tamasic.

claim: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheer, savoury, smooth, firm and pleasant, are dear to the sattvic.

cultivates.why: food chosen for clarity and cheer

commentary.reading: Foods that promote life, energy, strength, health, happiness and satisfaction are liked by the sattvic; one can know one's own guna by one's taste in food.

claim: The wise renouncer, pervaded by sattva and free of doubt, neither hates disagreeable work nor clings to agreeable work.

heals.why: unpleasant work is done without hatred of it
doubts cut

cultivates.why: the same toward pleasant and unpleasant duty
no clinging to the congenial task

commentary.reading: He does not hate work that is unpleasant, nor is he attached to pleasant work; filled with sattva, wise, his doubts cut by knowledge of the self.

claim: The knowledge by which one sees one imperishable being in all beings, undivided in the divided, is sattvic.

heals.why: separateness is appearance; one undivided being runs through all

cultivates.why: one imperishable reality in every being
others are not finally other

commentary.reading: The knowledge that sees the one changeless self, undivided in all the divided bodies, is sattvic.

claim: Obligatory action done without attachment, without love or hate, by one not seeking its fruit, is sattvic.

heals.why: action is described with the craving for its fruit removed

cultivates.why: not driven by like or dislike
without clinging

commentary.reading: Obligatory action done without attachment, not prompted by love or hatred, by one who does not desire its fruit, is sattvic.

claim: Action done by one craving desires, or with ego, or with great strain, is called rajasic.

heals.why: huge strain is named as a sign of work driven by ego or craving, not of good work

cultivates.why: asks what is driving the effort

commentary.reading: Action done by one longing for its fruit, or with egoism, with great effort, is rajasic.

claim: Action begun from delusion, heedless of consequence, loss, injury and one's own capacity, is called tamasic.

cultivates.why: four things to weigh before acting: what follows, what it costs, whom it hurts, what one can carry

commentary.reading: Action started from non-discrimination, without regard to what follows, to loss, to harm to living beings, and to one's own ability, is tamasic.

claim: The doer who is passionate, eager for fruit, greedy, harmful, impure and swayed by joy and sorrow is called rajasic.

cultivates.why: being tossed by joy and grief over results is named as a mark of the driven doer

needs: a hard mirror; pairs 'tossed by joy and grief' with greed and harm

commentary.reading: Attached, desiring the fruit of action, covetous, given to injuring, impure, elated at success and grieved at failure: such a doer is rajasic.

claim: The intellect that knows dharma and adharma, duty and non-duty incorrectly is rajasic.

cultivates.why: a restless mind misjudges right and wrong; settle it before deciding

commentary.reading: The intellect by which one understands dharma and adharma, what should and should not be done, not as they are, is rajasic.

claim: The intellect that, wrapped in darkness, takes adharma for dharma and sees all things inverted is tamasic.

cultivates.why: the possibility that one's certainty is upside down

commentary.reading: Covered by tamas, the intellect regards adharma as dharma and understands all things contrary to what they are.

claim: The unswerving firmness by which one holds the activities of mind, breath and senses through yoga is sattvic.

cultivates.why: steadiness defined: holding mind, breath and senses on course
unwavering

commentary.reading: The firmness, always joined to concentration, by which the functions of mind, breath and senses are kept from going the wrong way, is sattvic.

claim: The firmness by which one holds to duty, pleasure and wealth with attachment, craving their fruit, is rajasic.

heals.why: persistence can itself be a form of craving

cultivates.why: asks what one's determination is in service of

commentary.reading: The firmness by which one holds fast to duty, pleasure and wealth, desiring their fruit as occasion arises, is rajasic.

claim: The firmness by which a dull-minded person does not let go of sleep, fear, grief, despondency and pride is tamasic.
needs: never as a mirror for grief or fear: it calls holding on to them dull-minded

commentary.reading: The firmness by which one of poor understanding does not give up sleep, fear, grief, dejection and arrogance is tamasic.

claim: Happiness is of three kinds; in the sattvic kind one comes to delight through practice and reaches the end of sorrow.

heals.why: there is a joy that is grown into, not found ready-made

cultivates.why: delight that comes through practice
practice is how it is reached

needs: read with 18.37

commentary.reading: Hear of the threefold happiness: that in which one delights by repeated practice and surely comes to the end of sorrow is described next.

claim: Happiness that deludes the self both at first and afterward, arising from sleep, laziness and heedlessness, is tamasic.

heals.why: the comfort of sleep and drift is named as a pleasure that dulls from start to finish
heedless ease is shown for what it does

cultivates.why: a third test of happiness: does it dull

commentary.reading: The happiness that deludes the self at the beginning and at the end, born of sleep, sloth and negligence, is tamasic.

claim: One with intellect unattached everywhere, self-mastered and free of longing attains by renunciation the supreme perfection of actionlessness.

cultivates.why: unattached everywhere
actionlessness is abiding as the actionless self

needs: a seeker far along

commentary.reading: With intellect unattached to sons, wife and the rest, self subdued, thirst gone, he attains by renunciation, that is by right knowledge, the supreme perfection of freedom from action.

line_issue: 'That's the highest freedom' drops both renunciation and actionlessness. Corrected: 'Unattached everywhere, self-mastered, free of longing, such a person reaches through renunciation the highest state, where nothing more needs doing.'

claim: Mentally resigning all actions to Krishna, holding him supreme and relying on buddhi yoga, one should keep the mind always on him.

heals.why: the work is inwardly handed over before it begins

cultivates.why: all actions resigned to him in the mind
him as the highest goal

needs: a devotional reader

commentary.reading: With discriminating mind give up all actions to the Lord; hold him as the supreme, resort to the yoga of steady understanding and keep the mind on him.

line_issue: 'The divine... it' removes the speaker. Corrected: 'In your heart, hand all your work to me. Hold me as your goal, lean on steady understanding, and keep your mind on me always.'

claim: Even sacrifice, giving and austerity should be done giving up attachment and fruit; this is Krishna's settled and highest view.

heals.why: even good works are done without a claim on their reward

cultivates.why: no clinging even to one's good deeds

needs: 'these actions' are sacrifice, giving and austerity (18.5)

commentary.reading: Even these purifying actions, sacrifice, gift and austerity, are to be done giving up attachment and their fruits; this is the Lord's definite and best view.

claim: Fixing the mind on Krishna, devoted, sacrificing and bowing to him, one comes to him; he promises this, for Arjuna is dear.

heals.why: 'you are dear to me', said by God to the one being taught
a promise of arriving, given on his word

cultivates.why: mind, love, worship and bowing all turned to him
'I promise you truly'

needs: a devotional reader; part of the closing word 18.64-66, best late in a plan

commentary.reading: Shankara: this is the most secret essence of karma yoga, devotion to the Lord alone; he makes a true promise because Arjuna is dear. Ramanuja reads it as the summit of bhakti yoga.

claim: Renouncing obligatory action is not proper; abandoning it out of delusion is declared tamasic.

cultivates.why: asks whether walking away comes from clear sight or from confusion

needs: a reader tempted to drop a duty in confusion; not for someone leaving harm or worn out by care

commentary.reading: Giving up obligatory action is not right for the unknowing, since it purifies; abandoning it through delusion is tamasic.

claim: Where Krishna, lord of yoga, and Arjuna the archer are, there are fortune, victory, prosperity and firm justice.

cultivates.why: conviction that where God and a ready human effort stand together, things go rightly
the Gita ends on confidence
victory and wellbeing are assured there

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Sanjaya's closing conviction: where the Lord of yoga and the bow-bearing Partha are, there fortune, victory, increase and unfailing right conduct abide. Later teachers draw the lesson of grace joined to effort.

line_issue: The line replaces Krishna and Arjuna with 'wisdom and skilled effort', an allegory the verse does not state. Corrected: 'Where Krishna, the lord of yoga, stands, and where Arjuna stands with his bow, there are fortune, victory, wellbeing and sure justice.'

claim: Obligatory work done simply because it ought to be done, giving up attachment and fruit, is sattvic renunciation.

heals.why: the reason for the work is that it is to be done; the payoff is left out of it

cultivates.why: attachment and fruit both given up
doing what must be done because it must be done

commentary.reading: When obligatory action is done because it ought to be done, giving up attachment and also the fruit, that renunciation is sattvic.

claim: The unreal has no being and the real never ceases to be; seers of truth have seen the conclusion about both.

heals.why: what is real in a person does not stop being
a test for telling the lasting from the passing

cultivates.why: discrimination of the real from the unreal
the real is that which never ceases

needs: a reflective reader

commentary.reading: The unreal, such as cold and heat with their causes, has no being; the real, the self, never ceases to be; the knowers of truth have ascertained both.

claim: Krishna asks whence this faintness came on Arjuna in a crisis: unworthy of the noble, barring heaven, and bringing disgrace.
needs: the scene: Krishna's first words to a great warrior who has just put down his bow; the teaching begins only after 2.7

commentary.reading: A rebuke meant to rouse Arjuna, before he has asked to be taught; Shankara begins his commentary only at 2.11. Plain sense as in Sridhara and Gita Press.

line_issue: The line keeps the question and drops the three hard words that make it a rebuke; shown alone it shames a struggling reader. Scene-bound only. Corrected: 'Where has this faintness come from, Arjuna, at such a moment? It is not worthy of you, and it leads nowhere good.'

claim: The self is called unmanifest, unthinkable and unchangeable; knowing it so, one should not grieve.

heals.why: the one who died was never the changeable thing that was seen

cultivates.why: the self is beyond the senses, beyond thought, beyond change

needs: some distance from the loss; ends with 'you should not grieve'

commentary.reading: Not an object of any sense, it is unmanifest; not an object of thought, unthinkable; without parts, unchangeable; knowing it thus you ought not to grieve.

line_issue: 'Ease your grief' softens 'you should not grieve'. That is kinder, but it changes the verse. Corrected: 'It is unseen, beyond thought, unchanging. Knowing it to be so, you need not grieve.'

claim: Even if one thinks the self constantly born and constantly dying, still one should not grieve so.

heals.why: the comfort does not depend on believing in a deathless self

cultivates.why: reasoning from the reader's own view of birth and death

needs: some distance from the loss; read with 2.27

commentary.reading: Granting, for argument, the common view that the self is born and dies with each body, even so grief is not fitting.

claim: The self dwelling in every body is eternal and cannot be slain; so one should not grieve for any being.

heals.why: what lived in the one who died cannot be destroyed
no being is finally lost

cultivates.why: the indweller of every body is deathless

needs: some distance from the loss; closes the teaching of 2.11-30

commentary.reading: The conclusion of the section: the embodied self in every body is eternally unslayable, so you ought not to grieve for any being, Bhishma and the rest.

claim: For those attached to pleasure and power, whose minds are carried away, a resolute understanding does not form in concentration.

heals.why: the mind cannot settle on one aim while it is chasing comfort and control
the cost of always wanting more is a mind that cannot gather itself

cultivates.why: sees what scatters resolve

commentary.reading: For those who cling to enjoyment and lordship, whose discrimination is stolen by flowery promises of them, the resolute understanding does not arise in the mind.

claim: The Vedas concern the three gunas; one should be beyond them, free of opposites, ever in sattva, unacquisitive and self-possessed.

heals.why: freedom from the urge to acquire and to hoard

cultivates.why: 'be possessed of the self'
free of the pairs of opposites
beyond the three qualities

needs: a seeker; not for someone under real money stress

commentary.reading: The Vedas' ritual portion concerns samsara made of the three gunas; be without desire, free of the pairs, established in sattva, without concern for getting and keeping, and vigilant.

line_issue: The line drops the Vedas, the three qualities and 'possessed of the self'. Corrected: 'Rise above the three qualities and the pull of opposites. Stay in clarity, free of the urge to get and to keep, and rooted in the self.'

claim: When the intellect crosses the mire of delusion, one grows dispassionate toward all heard and yet to be heard.

heals.why: the fog is something one crosses
the hunger for one more opinion falls away when understanding clears

cultivates.why: a clear understanding needs less input
dispassion toward more hearing

commentary.reading: When your intellect passes beyond the turbidity of delusion that confuses self and not-self, you will reach dispassion about what is heard and to be heard, seeing it as fruitless.

claim: Objects fall away from one who abstains, but the taste remains; even the taste ceases on seeing the Supreme.

heals.why: explains why abstaining alone leaves the craving alive, and what finally ends it
lingering taste after giving something up is expected

cultivates.why: restraint is not yet freedom
the taste goes when the highest is seen

commentary.reading: Even the ignorant ascetic's sense objects turn away, but not the relish for them; that subtle attachment ends only when the supreme reality, Brahman, is seen.

line_issue: 'Until something higher replaces it' turns seeing the Supreme into swapping habits. Corrected: 'Staying away from a craving removes its object, but the taste lingers. Even the taste falls away once the highest is seen.'

claim: Restraining all the senses, one should sit disciplined, intent on Krishna; wisdom is firm in one whose senses are controlled.

heals.why: gathering the senses and sitting with the mind on him

cultivates.why: wisdom is firm when the senses are in hand
sitting intent on him

commentary.reading: Shankara: having restrained them, sit intent on the Lord, thinking 'I am no other than he'. Ramanuja: the senses cannot be conquered without fixing the mind on the Lord, so the two go together.

line_issue: 'What's highest' removes 'intent on me'. Corrected: 'Gather in all the senses and sit steady, your mind on me. When the senses are in hand, wisdom stands firm.'

claim: In serenity all sorrows end; the understanding of the serene-minded soon becomes steady.

heals.why: sorrows end in a clear mind
clarity comes first and steadiness of understanding follows quickly

cultivates.why: serenity is the ground of both relief and steady judgement

needs: follows 2.64, which says how serenity is reached

commentary.reading: When there is serenity all sorrows are destroyed, for the intellect of the clear-minded soon becomes steady like space.

claim: What is night to all beings, the self-controlled sage is awake in; where beings are awake is night to the seeing sage.

heals.why: what everyone is chasing is not the measure
not caring for what the crowd cares for may be the start of another kind of waking

cultivates.why: the wise and the many are awake to different things
the sage is awake to the self

commentary.reading: The supreme reality is like night to all beings and the sage is awake in it; the world of duality in which beings are awake is night to the sage who sees.

claim: This is the state of Brahman; attaining it one is not deluded, and abiding in it even at death one reaches Brahman-nirvana.

heals.why: one established here is not lost even at the hour of death

cultivates.why: the state of Brahman
no delusion after reaching it

needs: a seeker reflecting on their own end; not for someone with an ill relative

commentary.reading: This is the state of abiding in Brahman after renouncing all; staying in it even in the last period of life one attains liberation in Brahman, how much more one who stays in it from youth.

line_issue: The line hides both Brahman and death. Corrected: 'This is the state of resting in Brahman. Having reached it, a person is no longer confused, and resting there even at the hour of death, finds the peace of Brahman.'

claim: Arjuna sees nothing that could remove the grief drying up his senses, not even an unrivalled kingdom or lordship over the gods.

depicts.why: 'this sorrow that is drying up my senses'
even winning everything would not touch it
he can see no remedy at all

commentary.reading: Plain sense, as in Shankara's introduction: Arjuna's grief and delusion are such that no worldly or heavenly gain could remove them; hence only knowledge of the self can.
commentary.source: Shankara, introduction to 2.11; Gita Press on 2.8

claim: By sacrifice humans should nourish the gods and the gods nourish them; nourishing one another, both attain the highest good.

cultivates.why: what sustains us is to be given back to
mutual nourishing as the order of things

commentary.reading: With sacrifice nourish the gods, Indra and the rest, and let them nourish you with rain and the like; thus sustaining each other you will reach the highest good.

line_issue: The line removes the gods and the offering, turning it into people nourishing each other. Corrected: 'Nourish the gods with your offering, and let the gods nourish you. Sustaining one another, you will reach the highest good.'

claim: The good who eat the remnants of sacrifice are freed from all sins; the wicked who cook for themselves alone eat sin.

heals.why: taking only for oneself is named as feeding on wrong

cultivates.why: offer and share first, then eat
one's food is first an offering

commentary.reading: Those who eat what is left after offering to the gods and the rest are freed from sins, including those of the household's five places of harm; those who cook only for themselves eat sin.

claim: For one who delights in the self, is satisfied in the self and content in the self alone, there is no duty.

heals.why: a contentment that does not depend on tasks or roles

cultivates.why: content in the self alone
delight in the self
the self is enough

commentary.reading: For the knower of the self, the renunciate whose delight and satisfaction are in the self and not in objects, there is nothing to be done.

line_issue: 'Nothing left to prove' is not 'no duty remains'. Corrected: 'For one who delights in the self, is satisfied by the self and content in the self alone, nothing remains that must be done.'

claim: As the unwise act attached to work, so the wise should act unattached, wishing the welfare of the world.

heals.why: energy for work can come from the good of others when personal ambition is gone

cultivates.why: acting to hold the world together
the same effort without the grip

commentary.reading: As the unknowing act with attachment to the fruit, the knower should act with the same diligence but unattached, wishing to protect the world.

claim: Knowledge is covered by desire, the constant enemy of the wise, an insatiable fire.

heals.why: desire is named as a fire that feeding never satisfies
'never enough' is its nature, not a sign that one more thing will do it

cultivates.why: knowing that desire clouds even the wise

commentary.reading: The wise know it as an enemy even while desiring, the ignorant only afterwards; hence it is the constant enemy of the wise, hard to fill, like fire.

claim: One should first control the senses and then cast off desire, the sinful destroyer of knowledge and realisation.

heals.why: a place to begin: the senses, before the craving has grown

cultivates.why: restraint at the first gate

needs: follows 3.40, which names senses, mind and intellect as desire's seat

commentary.reading: Therefore first restrain the senses and abandon this sinful one, desire, which destroys knowledge from scripture and teacher and its direct realisation.

claim: The senses are high; higher is the mind; higher than mind the intellect; and beyond the intellect is the self.

heals.why: there is a place in you above the level where craving operates
the mind is not the top of you

cultivates.why: the self stands beyond senses, mind and intellect
a ladder for locating oneself

commentary.reading: The senses are superior to the gross body, the mind to the senses, the intellect to the mind; and the one who is beyond the intellect, the witness, is the supreme self.

claim: One who controls the senses by the mind and, unattached, engages the organs of action in karma yoga excels.

heals.why: the alternative to forced withdrawal is to get to work with the senses guided

cultivates.why: senses steered by the mind
work without being hooked

needs: contrast with 3.6

commentary.reading: The unknowing one who restrains the senses by the mind and begins karma yoga with the organs of action, unattached, is better than the hypocrite of 3.6.

claim: Freed from passion, fear and anger, absorbed in Krishna and taking refuge in him, many purified by knowledge have attained his being.

heals.why: many before you have come free of fear
and of anger, by taking refuge in him

cultivates.why: absorbed in him, sheltering in him
the path has been walked by many

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Many, free of attachment, fear and anger, seeing no difference from the Lord and relying on him alone, purified by the austerity that is knowledge, have attained liberation.

line_issue: 'Found their way home' drops 'absorbed in me, taking refuge in me'. Corrected: 'Many have let go of craving, fear and anger, taken refuge in me, been made clean by knowledge, and come to me.'

claim: One must understand action, forbidden action and inaction; the way of action is hard to fathom.

heals.why: knowing what to do is hard by nature, and the teacher says so
confusion about the right act is not stupidity; the matter is deep

cultivates.why: three things to tell apart: what to do, what not to do, and not doing
invites careful study of action

commentary.reading: The true nature of enjoined action, forbidden action and inaction must be understood, for it is hard to know; 4.16 says even the wise are confused here.

claim: One who sees inaction in action and action in inaction is wise among people, a yogi who has done all action.

heals.why: there is a stillness that activity does not disturb

cultivates.why: the self does nothing even while body and mind act
mere idleness is still a kind of doing

needs: a reflective reader

commentary.reading: Action belongs to body and senses and is wrongly placed on the actionless self; one who sees the self as non-acting amid action, and sees that sitting idle is also an act of the body, is wise.

claim: Without expectation, mind and self controlled, all possessions given up, doing only bodily action, one incurs no fault.

heals.why: acting with no expectation attached

cultivates.why: possessiveness given up

needs: the tradition reads this of the renunciate

commentary.reading: The renunciate without desires, mind and body controlled, having given up all possessions, doing only what keeps the body alive, incurs no sin.

line_issue: 'You can work' hides that the verse speaks of only bodily upkeep after giving up all possessions. Corrected: 'Expecting nothing, mind and self in hand, all possessions let go, doing only what the body needs, such a person incurs no fault.'

claim: As blazing fire reduces fuel to ashes, the fire of knowledge reduces all actions to ashes.

heals.why: the hold of past actions is fuel that understanding burns up

cultivates.why: knowledge is stronger than what one has done
knowledge of the self ends the binding of deeds

needs: the burden is guilt for one's own acts

commentary.reading: The fire of knowledge makes all actions seedless, except those that have already begun to bear fruit in this body.

claim: Nothing here purifies like knowledge; one perfected in yoga finds it within oneself in time.

heals.why: there is a cleansing, and it is found within
'in time': it comes of itself to the one who keeps practising

cultivates.why: patience with one's own ripening
knowledge named as the highest purifier

commentary.reading: There is no purifier equal to knowledge; one made fit through karma yoga and the yoga of concentration finds it in himself after long time.

claim: Actions do not bind one who has renounced action through yoga, whose doubts knowledge has cut, and who is self-possessed.

heals.why: doubt is cut by knowledge

cultivates.why: self-possessed, not bound by what one does
knowledge as what cuts doubt

commentary.reading: One who has given up actions through the yoga of seeing the supreme truth, whose doubt is cut by knowledge of the oneness of self and Lord, and who is vigilant, is not bound.

claim: Yogis act with body, mind, intellect and senses alone, giving up attachment, for the purification of the self.

heals.why: work can be for becoming clear inside, which no outcome can take away
gives work an inner purpose

cultivates.why: work with attachment given up
purification of the mind as the aim

commentary.reading: 'Alone' means without the sense of 'mine' in body, mind, intellect and senses; yogis act so, giving up attachment to results, for purity of mind.

claim: Those whose minds rest in evenness have conquered birth here itself; Brahman is flawless and same, so they rest in Brahman.

cultivates.why: the mind established in sameness
evenness is resting in Brahman, which is the same in all

commentary.reading: Even while living, birth is overcome by those whose mind stays in the sameness of Brahman in all beings; Brahman is untouched by the defects of bodies.

line_issue: 'Already won' drops why: they rest in Brahman. Corrected: 'Those whose minds rest in evenness have overcome the world right here. Brahman is flawless and the same in all, and so they rest in Brahman.'

claim: Renunciation and karma yoga both lead to the highest good, but karma yoga is better than renunciation of action.

heals.why: both stepping back and acting rightly are honoured, and the verdict is given: act

cultivates.why: settles the stay-or-withdraw question toward engaged action

commentary.reading: Shankara: karma yoga is better than mere renunciation without knowledge; renunciation with knowledge is a separate matter. Ramanuja: karma yoga is easier and safer and contains knowledge within it.

claim: The yogi whose happiness, delight and light are within becomes Brahman and attains Brahman-nirvana.

heals.why: points to a happiness and light that are inside
one's delight is within, not dependent on company

cultivates.why: happy within, delighting within
the inner light is the self

commentary.reading: One whose joy, play and light are in the inner self alone becomes Brahman and attains liberation here while living.

claim: Seers whose sins are destroyed, doubts cut, selves controlled, who delight in the good of all beings, attain Brahman-nirvana.

cultivates.why: delight in the welfare of all beings
harmlessness toward all

commentary.reading: Seers of right vision, sins worn away, doubts cut, senses controlled, intent on the good of all and harming none, attain liberation.

claim: The sage with senses, mind and intellect controlled, intent on liberation, free of desire, fear and anger, is ever free.

heals.why: freedom from fear named as attainable
freedom from anger named with it

cultivates.why: desire, fear and anger gone
already free

needs: completes 5.27 on the practice of meditation

commentary.reading: The renunciate who shuts out outer contacts, controls senses, mind and intellect and is free of desire, fear and anger is always liberated; nothing further remains for him.

claim: When the mind restrained by yoga comes to rest, one sees the self by the self and is content in it.

heals.why: the mind does come to rest through practice

cultivates.why: seeing the self by the self
content in the self
the stilled mind

commentary.reading: When the mind, restrained by practice of yoga, withdraws, and one sees the self, the supreme light, by the purified inner organ, one is satisfied in the self.

claim: Supreme happiness comes to the yogi whose mind is tranquil, whose rajas is stilled, who is sinless and has become Brahman.

cultivates.why: the highest happiness comes to the quiet mind
passion stilled

commentary.reading: The highest happiness comes to this yogi of tranquil mind, whose rajas, the afflictions such as delusion, has subsided, who is free of taint and has become Brahman.

claim: The yogi sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self, seeing the same everywhere.

heals.why: no being is outside oneself

cultivates.why: the self in all and all in the self
equal vision everywhere
others seen as oneself

commentary.reading: One whose mind is absorbed in yoga sees his own self present in all beings from Brahma to a clump of grass, and all beings as one with the self.

claim: Arjuna says he cannot see this yoga of evenness lasting, because of the mind's restlessness.

depicts.why: 'I cannot see it lasting; my mind is too restless'
he doubts the teaching can hold for him

commentary.reading: Arjuna, seeing how hard the yoga of right vision is, says he does not see its steady continuance because the mind is fickle.

claim: Reborn, the fallen yogi regains the understanding of his former body and strives again, harder, for perfection.

heals.why: what was gained is not lost with an interruption
a broken effort is picked up again from where it stopped

cultivates.why: strives again, more than before
effort is kept

needs: the verse speaks of carrying practice across births; the app line applies it within one life

commentary.reading: In that birth he regains the understanding acquired in the earlier body and strives more intensely than before for perfection.

line_issue: The line drops rebirth, which is the verse's actual claim. Corrected: 'What was learned in an earlier life is not lost. It returns, and the seeker strives again, harder than before.'

claim: By former practice the fallen yogi is carried on even helplessly; even the mere inquirer into yoga goes beyond Vedic rite.

heals.why: past practice has momentum that carries you when willingness is missing

cultivates.why: earlier effort keeps working
even the wish to know counts

needs: the context is rebirth of one who fell from yoga

commentary.reading: He is drawn on by the force of the earlier practice even against his will; even one who only wishes to know yoga rises above the fruit of Vedic ritual.

claim: The yogi striving diligently, cleansed of sin and perfected through many births, then reaches the highest goal.

heals.why: the long road does arrive

cultivates.why: perfection is gathered little by little over a long time
keep striving

commentary.reading: Gathering a little merit in each of many births, the striving yogi becomes perfected and then, with right vision, reaches the highest goal.

claim: The yogi satisfied by knowledge and realisation, unshaken, senses conquered, to whom clod, stone and gold are alike, is called steadfast.

heals.why: gold has no more pull than a stone on one who is satisfied within

cultivates.why: satisfied by knowledge and its realisation
earth, stone and gold alike

needs: a seeker's ideal; not for someone short of money

commentary.reading: Knowledge is understanding what scripture teaches and vijnana is making it one's own experience; satisfied by these, unshakeable, he is called established in yoga.

line_issue: The line keeps only the gold image and drops what makes it true. Corrected: 'The yogi who is satisfied by knowledge and by living it, unshaken, master of the senses, to whom a lump of earth, a stone and gold are the same, is called steadfast.'

claim: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith, Krishna makes that very faith unwavering.

heals.why: one's own chosen form of worship is supported by God himself

cultivates.why: faith in whatever form is steadied by him

needs: a reader open to God; 7.20-23 add that such worshippers gain limited fruits

commentary.reading: Whatever divine form a desirous devotee wishes to worship with faith, the Lord makes firm that same faith; the fruit they get is finite (7.23).

claim: All beings fall into delusion at birth through the delusion of opposites arising from desire and aversion.

heals.why: confusion is the common starting condition, produced by liking and disliking
aversion is named as half of what clouds sight

cultivates.why: seeing like and dislike as the source of confusion

commentary.reading: By the delusion of the pairs, born of desire for the pleasant and aversion to the unpleasant, the intellect of all beings is overpowered from birth, so knowledge of the self does not arise.

claim: With a mind disciplined by practice and not straying elsewhere, constantly meditating, one goes to the supreme divine Person.

heals.why: practice is what trains the mind not to stray

cultivates.why: a mind made steady by repetition
constant thought of the supreme Person

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Practice is the repetition of the same thought of the Lord, unbroken by other thoughts; with a mind so engaged, one reaches the supreme Person.

line_issue: 'You reach what you meditate on' removes the supreme Person. Corrected: 'With a mind trained by practice and not wandering elsewhere, thinking of him always, one reaches the supreme divine Person.'

claim: Fixing mind on Krishna, devoted, sacrificing and bowing to him, united and holding him as the goal, one comes to him.

heals.why: a way of joining oneself to him is given

cultivates.why: mind, love, worship and bowing turned to him
'you will come to me'

needs: a devotional reader

commentary.reading: Shankara: with mind on the Lord, devoted, worshipping and bowing to him, having steadied the mind, with him as the supreme goal, you will reach him, the self. Repeated at 18.65 with a promise.

claim: Since action has five causes, one who through untrained understanding sees the self alone as doer does not see.

heals.why: a failure was never made by you alone
a success was never made by you alone
'I alone did it' is named as not seeing

cultivates.why: seeing all the causes of an act
the pure self is not the doer

needs: read with 18.14, the five causes

commentary.reading: One who, with an intellect untrained by scripture and teacher, sees the pure actionless self as the agent, when the five causes are the agents, does not see; he is of perverted understanding.

claim: For those whose minds are set on Krishna, he soon becomes the deliverer from the ocean of death-bound samsara.

heals.why: 'I lift them out', and soon
to someone going under, a rescuer is promised
the rescue is his doing

cultivates.why: the mind rested in him
deliverance promised
'before long'

needs: a devotional reader; the sea is death and rebirth, so not for someone with an ill relative

commentary.reading: Shankara: for those who worship him with all actions offered, the Lord himself soon lifts them out of the ocean of samsara marked by death. Ramanuja stresses that he does it without delay because he cannot bear their separation.

line_issue: 'The drowning sea' hides that the sea is death and rebirth. Corrected: 'Whoever rests their heart in me, I soon lift out of the sea of death and endless return.'

claim: Arjuna asks Krishna to cut this doubt completely, for no one but Krishna can remove it.

depicts.why: a doubt he cannot settle himself
'there is no one else I can ask'

cultivates.why: taking one's doubt to the one who can answer it

commentary.reading: No sage or god other than the Lord can destroy this doubt, so he alone should cut it.

claim: With mind attached to Krishna, practising yoga under his refuge, one will know him fully and without doubt.

heals.why: full knowing, without doubt, is promised to the one who stays attached and keeps practising

cultivates.why: leaning on him as refuge
the promise of knowing him fully

needs: a devotional reader

commentary.reading: With mind fixed on the Lord, taking him alone as refuge and practising yoga, you will know him completely, with his powers and glory, without doubt.

claim: Nothing is higher than Krishna; all this is strung on him like gems on a thread.

heals.why: nothing is loose or random; everything hangs on one thread
what holds everything also holds this change

cultivates.why: one thread through all things
he is what all rests on

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: There is no other cause beyond the supreme Lord; all beings and the whole universe are woven on him like cloth on threads, like beads on a string.

claim: All four kinds of devotee are noble, but the wise one, steadfast and resorting to Krishna alone, is his very self.

heals.why: whoever turns to him, even from need, is called noble
coming to God out of trouble is honoured

cultivates.why: every devotee is noble in his eyes
the one who takes him as the only goal is his own self

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: all are noble, but the knower is the Lord's very self, not other than him. Ramanuja: the Lord cannot sustain himself without such a devotee, so he calls him his self.

line_issue: 'The one who loves me' replaces 'the wise one' (jnani). Corrected: 'All who turn to me, even in need, are noble. But the one who knows me and holds to me alone, I count as my very self.'

claim: As the mighty wind moving everywhere always rests in space, so all beings rest in Krishna.

heals.why: even ceaseless movement happens inside a stillness that holds it
wherever one is blown, one is still held

cultivates.why: all beings rest in him
the sky is not disturbed by the wind in it

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: As the great wind, going everywhere, stays always in space without touching it, so all beings stay in the Lord, who is all-pervading like space, without contact.

claim: Krishna will speak his supreme word again for Arjuna's good, because Arjuna delights in it and is dear.

heals.why: the teacher speaks because the listener is dear to him
someone wishes your good and says so

cultivates.why: the teaching is given out of love

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: The Lord speaks again of his own accord, wishing Arjuna's good, because Arjuna is delighted by his words as by drinking nectar.

claim: Arjuna asks the immeasurable Lord's forgiveness for disrespect shown in jest at play, rest, seat or meals, alone or in company.

depicts.why: every careless joke and slight is remembered and owned

cultivates.why: asking forgiveness plainly, with nothing held back

needs: the feeling of having taken someone for granted; the scene is the cosmic form

commentary.reading: Plain sense, shared by the commentators: Arjuna begs pardon for slights made in fun while walking, resting, sitting and eating. This record duplicates the second half of bg.11.41 in the library.

claim: By undivided devotion alone Krishna can be known in this form, seen in truth and entered into.

cultivates.why: devotion that looks to nothing else
he can be known, seen and entered

needs: a devotional reader

commentary.reading: Not by Vedas, austerity, gifts or sacrifice, but by devotion that turns to nothing other than the Lord, he can be known from scripture, seen directly and entered, which is liberation.

claim: Those who fix their minds on Krishna and worship him ever united, with supreme faith, he deems the best yogis.

cultivates.why: supreme faith
the mind rested in him, always

needs: a devotional reader

commentary.reading: Answering 12.1: those who worship the Lord in his form with mind fixed and highest faith are the best yogis. Shankara notes the worshippers of the imperishable also reach him (12.3-4); Ramanuja takes devotion to the personal Lord as plainly superior.

claim: Those who resign all actions to Krishna, hold him supreme and worship him in single-minded meditation, he soon delivers from samsara.

heals.why: the work is laid in him and the rescue is his
deliverance from the sea of death is promised
the load of doing is handed over

cultivates.why: all actions laid in him
he becomes the deliverer

needs: a devotional reader; the record joins 12.6 and 12.7, so it overlaps bg.12.7

commentary.reading: Shankara: for those who offer all actions to the Lord and meditate on him with undivided yoga, he becomes before long the lifter out of the ocean of mortal samsara.

line_issue: 'The drowning sea' hides that the sea is death and rebirth. Corrected: 'Lay all your work in me and keep your mind on me. I soon lift such a person out of the sea of death and endless return.'

claim: Krishna is the goal, sustainer, lord, witness, abode, refuge and friend, the origin, dissolution, ground, treasury and imperishable seed.

heals.why: 'I am your home, your shelter, your friend'
the one who holds origin and ending is also the witness and the refuge
a shelter that does not end

cultivates.why: he is the refuge
home and shelter are in him
a friend who witnesses everything

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: He is the fruit of action, the nourisher, the master, the witness of what beings do and leave undone, the dwelling, the refuge of the afflicted, and the friend who helps without return.

claim: Krishna is the father, mother, sustainer and grandfather of this world, the knowable, the purifier, Om and the three Vedas.

heals.why: the world has a father and a mother who does not leave
for one who has lost a parent: a parenthood that remains

cultivates.why: he holds the world up as a parent does
turning to him as to father and mother

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: He is the father and mother of the world, the dispenser of the fruits of action, the grandfather, the thing to be known, the purifier and the syllable Om.

claim: For the ever-united yogi who remembers Krishna constantly with undivided mind, Krishna is easy to reach.

heals.why: he is easy to reach for the one who keeps remembering
no feat is required, only remembrance

cultivates.why: constant remembrance
'I am easy to reach'

needs: a devotional reader

commentary.reading: For the yogi who remembers the Lord without break, for as long as he lives, with mind on nothing else, the Lord is easily attained.

claim: Having spoken, Krishna showed his own form again and, becoming gentle, comforted the frightened Arjuna.

heals.why: God sees the fear and changes his own form to comfort it; he does not argue with it

cultivates.why: comfort given to the frightened one
he is gentle with those who are afraid

needs: the scene of the cosmic form

commentary.reading: Plain sense: Vasudeva showed again the form born in Vasudeva's house and, with a gentle body, consoled the terrified Arjuna.

claim: Seeing Krishna's gentle human form, Arjuna is composed again and restored to his own nature.

depicts.why: 'I have come to myself; I am back to my nature', said in relief after terror
calm returning at the sight of a familiar, gentle face

needs: the scene of the cosmic form

commentary.reading: Plain sense: seeing the gentle human form, Arjuna says his mind is collected and he has returned to his natural state.

claim: Even while always doing all actions, one who takes refuge in Krishna attains by his grace the eternal, imperishable abode.

heals.why: the work continues, but it is done leaning on him
daily work is given a destination

cultivates.why: leaning on him while working
the end is reached by grace

needs: a devotional reader

commentary.reading: Even one who always does all actions, taking the Lord as his whole refuge, attains by the Lord's grace the eternal state.

claim: The Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, making them revolve by his maya as if mounted on a machine.

heals.why: the Lord is in one's own heart
one is moved by a power larger than one's will

cultivates.why: 18.62 follows: take refuge in him alone
he is present within every being

needs: a reader open to God; the second half can read as 'you are a puppet' without 18.62

commentary.reading: The Lord, the ruler, abides in the heart region of all beings and by his maya makes them turn like wooden figures mounted on a machine.

line_issue: The line drops the second half of the verse. Corrected: 'The Lord lives in the heart of every being, Arjuna, and by his power moves them all, as though they were set on a wheel.'

claim: Krishna will again speak his supreme and most secret word for Arjuna's good, because Arjuna is firmly beloved to him.

heals.why: 'you are firmly dear to me', said by God
loved, and told so
the love is declared before any condition is set

cultivates.why: the final teaching is given out of love
prepares the heart for 18.65-66

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: the Lord repeats the most secret teaching not from fear or for gain but because Arjuna is firmly dear. Ramanuja: it introduces the final word on devotion.

claim: Krishna's divine maya of the three gunas is hard to cross; those who take refuge in him alone cross it.

heals.why: the confusion is named as truly hard to get through, and a way through is given
effort alone was never expected to be enough

cultivates.why: taking refuge in him alone
those who do, cross

needs: a reader open to God

commentary.reading: Shankara: this maya, made of the gunas and belonging to the Lord, is hard to overcome; those who give up all else and take refuge in him alone, their own self, cross it. Ramanuja: surrender is the only means of crossing.

line_issue: 'This tangle' drops that it is God's own power made of the three qualities. Corrected: 'This divine power of mine, woven of the three qualities, is hard to get past. Those who take refuge in me alone cross beyond it.'

claim: Fixing the mind and settling the intellect in Krishna alone, one will dwell in him thereafter, without doubt.

heals.why: the mind is given one place to rest
'you will live in me'

cultivates.why: mind and understanding placed in him
'of this there is no doubt'

needs: a devotional reader; 12.9-11 give easier steps for one who cannot

commentary.reading: Fix the mind, which thinks, and the intellect, which decides, on the Lord in his cosmic form; after the body falls you will dwell in him as his self, without doubt.

claim: Whoever holds 'I am free' is free and whoever holds 'I am bound' stays bound; one's understanding decides one's end.

heals.why: the sense of being bound and small is shown to rest on a notion about oneself
shame that has hardened into 'this is what I am' loosens when bondage is seen as a belief

cultivates.why: points to the self that was never bound

needs: the reader must take 'free' and 'bound' as statements about the self, not about outer circumstances

commentary.reading: Advaita: bondage and liberation are superimposed notions; the self is ever free, so taking oneself as bound is the bondage. It is a claim about the self, not a technique of positive thinking.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened; reading is the standard Advaita sense of the text, recalled

line_issue: 'As you think, so you become' reads as manifestation and can tell a person facing real constraints that their thinking is to blame. Corrected: 'Whoever holds I am free is free, and whoever holds I am bound stays bound. The old saying is true: as your understanding is, so is where you arrive.'

claim: Be free of expectation, unchanging, self-reliant, cool at heart, deep and unshaken, resting in pure awareness alone.

heals.why: offers a mind that is cool and unshaken as the place to stand
nirapeksha, needing nothing from outside, is the first quality named

cultivates.why: unshaken, unchanging is the posture held up
a cool heart resting in awareness

needs: accepts awareness as what one is

commentary.reading: Advaita: these are marks of one who rests as consciousness; they follow from knowing the self rather than being moods to manufacture.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: If you want freedom, shun sense objects like poison and take forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth like nectar.

heals.why: the objects of craving are to be avoided like poison
contentment is one of the five nectars

cultivates.why: forgiveness is named first among the nectars
contentment is to be drunk like nectar
daya, kindness, is one of the five

needs: the reader wants freedom; the verse is the first instruction to one who has asked

commentary.reading: Ashtavakra's opening reply: dispassion toward sense objects and the five virtues are the preparation for knowledge. Vishaya means the objects themselves, not only the craving.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The verse says shun the sense objects themselves like poison; the line narrows it to craving. Corrected: 'If you want freedom, leave the objects of craving as you would poison, and take forgiveness, honesty, kindness, contentment and truth as nectar.'

claim: If you set the body apart and rest in awareness, you will be happy, at peace and free this very moment.

heals.why: the promise is peace now, not after the problem is solved
resting in awareness is offered as a place the restless mind can stop

cultivates.why: peace is promised now
the self is taken as awareness, distinct from the body

needs: accepts that one is awareness, distinct from the body

commentary.reading: Advaita: discriminating the self from the body (deha-atma viveka) and abiding as consciousness is liberation itself, available immediately.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: 'I am the doer' is the bite of ego's black snake; drink the nectar of trust that you are not the doer, and be happy.

heals.why: the doer-sense itself is named as the poison
the weight of carrying every outcome falls away with the doer-sense

cultivates.why: vishvasa, trust, is the nectar offered

needs: accepts the Advaita claim that the self does not act

commentary.reading: Advaita: doership belongs to body and mind; the self is akarta. Freedom comes from knowing this, not from doing less.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line softens the proposition to 'not the only doer'; the verse says the self is not the doer at all. Corrected: 'The thought I am the doer is the bite of a great black snake. Drink the nectar of trust that says I am not the doer, and be happy.'

claim: Wherever craving is, the round of becoming is there; take up mature dispassion, be free of craving and be happy.

heals.why: craving is named as the very place where samsara lives
dispassion is offered as the way out

cultivates.why: praudha vairagya, ripe dispassion, is prescribed

commentary.reading: Samsara is not a place but the presence of thirst; ripe dispassion is the remedy.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Enough of wealth, desire and even good deeds; in the wilderness of the world the mind never found rest in them.

depicts.why: the weariness of having had wealth, pleasure and merit and found no rest in any
a mind that has run through the wilderness and is tired

cultivates.why: the weariness is the ground of letting go

commentary.reading: Spoken to turn Janaka's tiredness with pursuits into dispassion; even dharmic deeds are no resting place for the mind.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: One certain that suffering here comes from worry alone, and nothing else, is free of it, happy and at peace.

heals.why: names worry as the source of the suffering

cultivates.why: one free of worry is at peace everywhere

needs: the reader's trouble is mostly rumination, not a present danger or loss

commentary.reading: Chinta here is mental ideation; Advaita holds that sorrow is born of the mind's constructions, not of the world.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened
