claim: You are the boundless ocean; let the waves of the world rise or fall, you neither grow nor shrink.

heals.why: worth does not shrink with a loss of role or status
the waves can rise and fall without touching the ocean

cultivates.why: gain and loss are waves
the self as the ocean in which the world rises

needs: accepts the self as awareness in which the world appears

commentary.reading: Advaita: the world is a natural play of waves on the ocean of consciousness and adds nothing to or takes nothing from the self.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Do not stir the mind with yes and no; grow still and rest happily in your own self, whose form is joy.

heals.why: sankalpa and vikalpa, the to and fro of the mind, are what is set down
the churn of yes and no

cultivates.why: upashama, stilling
the self is called ananda-vigraha

commentary.reading: Sankalpa-vikalpa is the mind's activity of willing and doubting; the instruction is to rest as the self, not to suppress decisions.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line drops that the rest is in one's own joyful self. Corrected: 'Do not churn your mind with yes and no. Grow still and rest at ease in your own self, which is joy.'

claim: Liberation is losing the taste for sense objects and bondage is relishing them; that is all there is to know.

heals.why: names relish for objects as the bond

cultivates.why: liberation is defined as the taste going

commentary.reading: A compressed definition: moksha is distaste for objects. 'Do as you wish' assumes that knowledge has removed the relish.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: You are not the body, nor is it yours; not the doer or enjoyer but awareness, the ever-present witness. Live happily.

heals.why: the self is not what failed or was judged
shame belongs to the doer, which the self is not

cultivates.why: awareness, the witness, is named as what you are

needs: accepts the witness teaching

commentary.reading: Advaita: the self is sakshi, neither agent nor experiencer; agency and enjoyment are superimposed by the mind.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line adds 'achievements' and drops doer and enjoyer, the core of the claim. Corrected: 'You are not the body, and the body is not yours. You are not the doer or the enjoyer. You are awareness, the witness that needs nothing. Live happily.'

claim: Liking and disliking belong to the mind, and you are never the mind; you are awareness, changeless. Live happily.

heals.why: aversion is placed in the mind, not in the self
the heat of dislike is something seen, not what one is

cultivates.why: the self as awareness free of thought-forms
changelessness

needs: accepts the witness teaching

commentary.reading: Raga and dvesha are dharmas of the antahkarana; the self is nirvikalpa bodha.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: The body made of the gunas comes, stays and goes; the self neither comes nor goes, so why grieve for it?

heals.why: grief is answered by the self that does not go

cultivates.why: the self is beyond coming and going

needs: the reader must already hold the self as deathless; a fresh griever hears 'stop grieving'

commentary.reading: The same argument as Gita 2.11-30: grief is for what is not the self. Here the grief questioned is grief for oneself as much as for another.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened; parallel to Shankara on Gita 2.11 recalled

claim: Everyone is miserable from straining, yet no one sees it; by this one teaching the fortunate find peace.

depicts.why: the exhausted straining that no one notices in themselves

heals.why: names the straining itself as the cause of the misery

cultivates.why: nirvriti, peace, follows on seeing it

commentary.reading: In chapter 16 ayasa covers all effort, even study and meditation; Ashtavakra says no striving yields the self.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: The attached one wants to leave the world to escape pain; the unattached has no pain and is untroubled even in it.

heals.why: the pain is traced to attachment, not to place
the urge to run is seen as attachment in another form

cultivates.why: freedom from raga makes place irrelevant

needs: the reader is not in a harmful situation; for someone being harmed leaving is right

commentary.reading: Aimed at the seeker who wants to renounce out of aversion: aversion is still raga. Freedom is inner, so neither fleeing nor staying matters.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Rare is one who does not dwell on pleasures enjoyed or long for those not yet had.

heals.why: names replaying old pleasures and pining for new ones
longing for what has not come

cultivates.why: the rare one is content with what is

commentary.reading: Part of the portrait of the jnani in chapter 17: freedom from memory and anticipation of enjoyment.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: The calm mind runs neither to crowds nor to the forest; whatever and wherever, it stays the same.

heals.why: the urge to change place to feel better

cultivates.why: sama, the same everywhere
needs neither company nor solitude

commentary.reading: The jnani is not defined by renunciation of society or by society; place is irrelevant to the settled mind.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: One may gain all wealth and abundant pleasure, yet without giving up everything no one is happy.

heals.why: gaining everything is shown not to bring happiness
the more is never the end

cultivates.why: sarva-parityaga, letting go of all

commentary.reading: Sarva-parityaga is read in Advaita as giving up the sense of ownership and doership, an inner renunciation; the text does not specify.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: 'Until you let go' softens 'without giving up everything'. Corrected: 'You may earn every kind of wealth and enjoy every pleasure, and still no one is happy without letting go of everything.'

claim: For a heart scorched by the blazing sun of things one must do, where is happiness without the cooling rain of calm?

depicts.why: the burning weight of 'I still have to do this'
the endless list of obligations

cultivates.why: prashama, calm, is the rain that cools

commentary.reading: Kartavya-duhkha is the pain of the sense of obligation that arises from doership; the cure is calm born of knowledge.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: The deluded never find peace because they are trying to get it; the wise, sure of the truth, are always calm.

heals.why: the effort to quiet the mind keeps it moving
names the trying itself as the obstacle

cultivates.why: calm follows clear knowing, not effort
tattva-nishchaya, certainty of truth

commentary.reading: Peace sought as an object stays out of reach; it is the nature of the self, revealed by knowledge.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: The confused are agitated even doing nothing; the skilful stay calm even while doing all that must be done.

heals.why: the agitation is shown to be in the mind, not in the work
busyness itself is not the cause

cultivates.why: calm amid full activity

commentary.reading: Inaction is not peace and action is not agitation; the difference lies in the mind.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: The calm-minded sit, sleep, come, go, speak and eat at ease, even in the business of daily life.

cultivates.why: calm inside ordinary activity
sukham is repeated six times

commentary.reading: A portrait of the jnani in vyavahara: ordinary life lived without agitation.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The verse describes the calm person; the line makes it a set of instructions. Corrected: 'The calm-minded sit at ease and sleep at ease, come and go at ease, speak and eat at ease, even in the middle of daily life.'

claim: The steady one neither prays for gain nor grieves loss; his cool mind is filled as if with nectar.

heals.why: asking for gain is set down
outcome worry about gain and loss

cultivates.why: a mind full without gain
same in gain and loss

commentary.reading: Portrait of the dhira: neither prayer for gain nor sorrow at its absence.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Praised, he is not pleased; blamed, not angry; he neither dreads death nor delights in living.

heals.why: blame does not anger him

cultivates.why: same in praise and blame
no dread of death

commentary.reading: Portrait of the jnani; the evenness toward death and life follows from not identifying with the body.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line adds 'That is freedom' and drops 'nor clings to life'. Corrected: 'Praised, he is not pleased. Blamed, he is not angry. He neither dreads death nor clings to life.'

claim: One who watches his own active body as if it were someone else's cannot be shaken by praise or blame.

heals.why: blame lands on the body-mind being watched, not on the watcher

cultivates.why: unshaken by praise and blame

needs: accepts the witness stance

commentary.reading: Chapter 3 tests Janaka: one who sees the body's activity as another's (the witness stance) cannot be disturbed.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Knowing 'I am That in which the world rises like waves', why do you run about like a beggar?

heals.why: the beggar's stance is called inconsistent with what one is
running for more

cultivates.why: I am That in which the world rises

needs: the reader claims self-knowledge; Ashtavakra is testing Janaka

commentary.reading: A test of Janaka's claimed realisation: if you know, why still behave like one in need? The barb is for one who says he knows.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Bondage is the mind wanting, grieving, grabbing, dropping, delighting or raging; freedom is the mind doing none of these.

heals.why: wanting is named as bondage
raging is named as bondage

cultivates.why: a mind that neither takes up nor throws off

commentary.reading: Bondage and freedom are states of the mind's movement; even grieving and renouncing are listed as bondage.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: The pairs of done and not-done have never come to rest for anyone; knowing this, through weariness, turn to renunciation.

depicts.why: the list of done and not-done that never ends

heals.why: seeing that the list never ends for anyone loosens its grip

cultivates.why: nirveda turned into letting go

commentary.reading: Kritakrita dvandvas never cease; the conclusion is tyaga-para avrati, intent on renunciation and free even of vows and observances.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: 'Ease your grip' softens the second half, which tells the seeker to become intent on renunciation and free even of vows. Corrected: 'Done and not yet done: for whom, and when, has that ever come to rest? Knowing this, grow weary of it and give yourself to letting go, bound by no vow.'

claim: No time or age of life is free of opposites; let them be, live with what comes, and you reach fulfilment.

heals.why: ups and downs are shown to belong to every stage of life
waiting for a calmer season to begin is answered

cultivates.why: upeksha, letting the pairs be
yatha-prapta-varti, living with what comes

commentary.reading: Yatha-prapta-vartin is the renunciate who lives on whatever comes unasked; in a householder setting it reads as acceptance of what arrives.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Friend mind, why so much chatter; it is all speculation. The essence is this: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.

heals.why: the mind's chatter is addressed as a friend and set aside
worry is named as vitarka, speculation

cultivates.why: you are tattva, sky-like
a light, friendly tone toward one's own mind

commentary.reading: Dattatreya addresses his own mind as sakhe, friend, and tells it the essence: the self is gagana-upama, sky-like, untouched by the mind's movements.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Do not weigh whether a teacher is young, worldly, unlearned, a servant or a householder; no one throws away a jewel fallen in dirt.

heals.why: pride that refuses wisdom from a lowly source

cultivates.why: take the jewel, not the wrapping

commentary.reading: On the guru: wisdom is to be accepted whatever the status or conduct of the one who gives it, as Dattatreya learned from his 24 teachers.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Look not for poetic merit but take the essence; an unpainted boat still carries across those who wish to cross.

heals.why: substance carries people across without polish

cultivates.why: sara-grahi, taking the essence

needs: the verse is about reading this text; applying it to one's own worth is an extension

commentary.reading: Dattatreya excuses the plain style of his own verses: the wise take the essence. It is a statement about the text.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The verse defends the plain style of the Avadhuta Gita itself; the line is fine as wording but should not be served as a claim about the reader's worth without that note.

claim: The free sage is alert, deep, steadfast, master of hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, age and death; humble, honouring others, friendly, kind, wise.

heals.why: amani, seeking no honour
honouring others rather than oneself

cultivates.why: maitra, friendly
karunika, compassionate
dhritiman, steadfast

commentary.reading: A list of the sadhu's marks; the same line appears as Bhagavata Purana 11.11.31 in Krishna's description of the saint (recalled, not verified).
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened; Bhagavata parallel recalled

line_issue: The line turns a portrait into instructions and drops mastery of the six waves (hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, age, death). Corrected: 'Alert and deep, steadfast, master of hunger, thirst, grief, delusion, age and death; wanting no honour yet honouring others; capable, friendly, kind and wise.'

claim: The syllable va marks one who has left old cravings, whose speech is wholesome, and who lives in the present.

heals.why: living in the present
vasanas given up

cultivates.why: dwelling in what is present

commentary.reading: One of the four syllables of avadhuta (a, va, dhu, ta) explained as a mark of the free person.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: Description of a mark turned into a command, acceptable in an act slot; for an opener keep it descriptive: 'Free of old cravings, wholesome in speech, living in the present: that is the mark of va.'

claim: Freed from wrongs like the moon from clouds, spotless, awaiting his time, the steady one succeeds through fortitude.

heals.why: waiting is framed as part of succeeding
steadiness, not speed, decides

cultivates.why: dhairya is named as the means

commentary.reading: Gita Press Hindi: the pure, steady person, freed from sin like the moon from clouds, waits patiently on time and attains siddhi. In the Shanti Parva moksha setting siddhi most likely means spiritual perfection, not worldly success.
commentary.source: Gita Press Hindi translation in raw_json/hans_gita_source.json checked; Nilakantha not opened

line_issue: The line makes this a promise of worldly success after waiting; the verse ties success to first being freed from wrongs and means spiritual attainment in its setting. Corrected: 'Freed from wrongs as the moon slips out of the clouds, clear and steady, the wise one waits on time and through patience reaches the goal.'

claim: The wise should take insult as contentedly as nectar; the insulted sleeps in peace while the one who insults is ruined.

heals.why: the hurt is set beside the fact that the insulter carries the ruin
no need to answer the insult in kind

cultivates.why: forbearance under insult
the insulted sleeps at ease

needs: the reader is past the first hurt and wants to stop carrying it; never as the first word to someone being mistreated

commentary.reading: A brahmana's ethic of forbearance; the same verse appears in Manusmriti 2.162-163 (recalled). The ruin of the insulter is stated as consequence, not wished.
commentary.source: plain sense in the Mahabharata context; Nilakantha not opened; Manu parallel recalled

claim: The world is covered by ignorance, envy keeps it from shining, greed makes people abandon friends, attachment keeps them from heaven.

heals.why: envy is named as what dims us
greed is named as how friends are lost

cultivates.why: four causes named plainly

commentary.reading: The swan's answer to the Sadhyas' question in Hamsa Gita 39 (verified in the Gita Press text). A near-identical pair appears in the Yaksha Prashna with tamasa for matsaryat (recalled).
commentary.source: Gita Press Hindi translation in raw_json/hans_gita_source.json checked; Nilakantha not opened

claim: The universe is pervaded by you and strung on you; by nature you are pure awareness, so do not fall into smallness of mind.

heals.why: the self is shown to be vast
comparison is a smallness of mind

cultivates.why: shuddha-buddha-svarupa, pure awareness

needs: accepts the self as pervading consciousness

commentary.reading: Advaita: the world is strung on consciousness like beads; kshudra-chittata is identifying with the limited mind.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: 'Wider than any worry' is invented and the pervading of the world is dropped. Corrected: 'This whole world is pervaded by you and strung on you. You are pure awareness by nature. Do not shrink into a small mind.'

claim: You belong to no caste or stage of life and are not an object of the senses; unattached, formless witness of all, be happy.

heals.why: labels of birth, role and appearance do not define the self
shame tied to identity or status loosens

cultivates.why: asanga, nirakara, vishva-sakshi

commentary.reading: The self is free of varna and ashrama identities, which belong to the body; one of the few self-level verses with no claim about death or an unreal world.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Through how many lives have you done painful, wearying work with body, mind and speech; now at least, let it cease.

depicts.why: lifetimes of tiring work with body, mind and speech

cultivates.why: uparama, ceasing

needs: the reader understands cessation as ceasing the doer-sense, not quitting duties

commentary.reading: Uparama is withdrawal from karma driven by desire; Advaita reads it as ceasing doership, not abandoning one's responsibilities.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: One certain that arising, change and ceasing happen by nature stays unchanged, free of pain, and easily finds peace.

heals.why: change is seen as nature, not as personal injury
uncertainty about change

cultivates.why: peace comes easily
nirvikara, unchanged

commentary.reading: Bhava-abhava-vikara arise from svabhava, nature; the knower does not take them as happening to the self.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: One certain that misfortune and fortune come in their time by destiny is content, senses at rest, neither longing nor grieving.

heals.why: outcomes are placed outside one's control
longing for good fortune is set down

cultivates.why: tripta, content

needs: accepts daiva, destiny

commentary.reading: Daiva is prarabdha: fortune and misfortune arrive as fruit of past karma; the knower neither longs nor grieves.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: 'On their own schedule' hides that the verse says destiny brings them. Corrected: 'Hard times and good times come in their time, by destiny. One sure of this is content, senses at rest, neither longing nor grieving.'

claim: The ease of owning nothing is rare even in a loincloth; so I have dropped both renouncing and acquiring and live at ease.

heals.why: acquiring is dropped
even pride in renouncing is dropped

cultivates.why: living yathasukham, at ease
freedom from both grabbing and giving up

commentary.reading: Janaka's song: outer renunciation does not give inner ease; the free one is beyond both tyaga and adana.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Seeing truly that nothing is ever really done by me, I do whatever comes to be done and live at ease.

heals.why: the weight of doership is lifted while the work still gets done
outcome worry ends with the doer-sense

cultivates.why: living yathasukham

needs: accepts non-doership

commentary.reading: Janaka's first-person song: knowing the self does not act, he does what presents itself without the sense of 'I did'.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line drops the ground of the verse, seeing that nothing is really done by me. Corrected: 'Seeing truly that nothing done is ever done by me, I do whatever comes to be done and live at ease.'

claim: A clear-minded person is fulfilled by a simple teaching; another stays confused after a lifetime of inquiry.

heals.why: endless inquiry is shown not to be the way
confusion that more reading does not cure

cultivates.why: a clear mind takes the teaching at once

commentary.reading: Sattva-buddhi, a pure intellect, grasps the teaching at once; a clouded one stays deluded however long it inquires.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Let the body last till the end of the age or go today; what gain or loss is that to you, pure awareness?

heals.why: fear of death answered by the self that is untouched

cultivates.why: chinmatra-rupa, pure awareness
no gain or loss to the self

needs: only for a seeker contemplating his own mortality; harmful to someone afraid for a sick parent or child

commentary.reading: Advaita: the body's span is indifferent to the self, which is pure consciousness.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Have faith, my son, have faith and do not be confused: you are knowledge itself, the Lord, the Self beyond nature.

heals.why: doubt is met with a twice-repeated 'have faith'
you are told you are the Lord, beyond nature

cultivates.why: shraddhasva, have faith
jnana-svarupa, the self beyond prakriti

commentary.reading: A tender, insistent assurance (tata, my dear) that the self is knowledge and Ishvara, beyond prakriti. Self-level without any claim about death or an unreal world.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line drops the identity the verse asserts (knowledge itself, the Lord, beyond nature) and replaces it with a vague 'more than everything that happens to you'. Corrected: 'Have faith, my child, have faith. Do not be confused about this. You are knowledge itself, the Lord, the Self beyond nature.'

claim: You may recite or hear many scriptures again and again, yet you will not be at ease until you forget them all.

heals.why: the pile of teachings is not what brings ease
a mind busy with doctrine

cultivates.why: svasthya, ease, comes from letting go of it all

needs: the reader is a seeker who reads a lot; it says nothing against learning for a student

commentary.reading: Sarva-vismarana, forgetting all, means dropping every mental construction including scriptural ones; it presupposes the teaching has been heard.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: One who is proud even of being liberated and possessive of the body is neither wise nor a yogi, only a sufferer.

heals.why: spiritual pride is named as suffering

cultivates.why: no mine-ness even toward the body

commentary.reading: Abhimana even about moksha and mamata toward the body mark one who has only words; he shares only in sorrow.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Enjoy, work or meditate as you will; your mind will still long most for the state where every want has dropped.

depicts.why: pleasure, work and even meditation have not given rest
the longing for a state beyond wanting

cultivates.why: the deepest wish is the end of wanting

commentary.reading: Whatever one does, only a mind free of all hopes truly satisfies; a direct statement of what the restless heart is seeking.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened; the Sanskrit can also read 'only a mind rid of all hopes will please you'

claim: One who is content, senses clear, and always happy alone has gained the fruit of knowledge and of yoga.

cultivates.why: tripta, content
ramate, delights in his own company

commentary.reading: Ekaki ramate is the jnani who delights in the self alone; it is a mark of attainment, not counsel to the lonely.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: Served to someone lonely or with an empty nest, the line reads as 'be happy alone'. Keep it for content or seeking readers; corrected wording: 'One who is content, clear in the senses and always happy in solitude has gained the fruit of knowledge and of yoga.'

claim: He neither longs for the world to end nor resents its going on; so the blessed one lives happily on whatever livelihood comes.

heals.why: no wish for it all to be over
no resentment toward life continuing

cultivates.why: content with whatever livelihood comes

commentary.reading: The jnani neither craves dissolution (moksha as escape) nor hates the world's continuance; he lives on whatever comes.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: For the steady yogi there is no difference between kingship and begging, gain and loss, the crowd and the forest.

heals.why: kingship does not inflate
begging does not diminish

cultivates.why: no vishesha, no difference

commentary.reading: Portrait of the nirvikalpa yogi: outer condition makes no difference to the settled mind.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: The steady one clings neither to doing nor to not doing; doing whatever comes to be done, he stays at ease.

heals.why: freed from the stuck question of whether to act
no stubborn grip on doing

cultivates.why: no durgraha either way
tishthati sukham

commentary.reading: Neither pravritti nor nivritti is grasped; the dhira does what presents itself. Same thought as 13.3.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Laughed at and scolded by servants, children, spouses, grandchildren and kin, the yogi is not disturbed in the least.

heals.why: mockery from family does not provoke

cultivates.why: no vikriti, no change

needs: never as advice to someone being mistreated at home

commentary.reading: Portrait of the yogi unmoved by contempt from his own household; descriptive of attainment.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line turns a portrait of the realised yogi into counsel to stay unshaken when family mocks you, which slides toward endurance of mistreatment. Corrected and descriptive: 'Laughed at and scolded by servants, children, spouse, grandchildren and kin, the yogi is not shaken in the least.'

claim: Even the deluded one's withdrawal turns into activity, while even the wise one's activity bears the fruit of stillness.

heals.why: rest that turns into busyness
work can carry stillness

cultivates.why: nivritti-phala inside activity

commentary.reading: Inner stillness, not outer inaction, decides; the mudha cannot rest even in retreat.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Beggar or king, whoever is free of desire shines, the one for whom things no longer look good or bad.

heals.why: worth does not depend on station
beggar and king shine alike

cultivates.why: nishkama
good and bad notions have fallen away

commentary.reading: Nishkamata, not station, is what makes one shine; the second half adds that judgements of good and bad have melted.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: The free one is at ease in any state, done with duty, even everywhere, and without craving does not recall what he did or left undone.

heals.why: the replay of done and undone falls away
no recalling of what was left undone

cultivates.why: sama sarvatra
yathasthiti-svastha

needs: the reader has already faced and repaired what they did; it does not excuse wrongdoing

commentary.reading: Portrait of the mukta, kritakartavya: having done what needed doing, he carries no memory-burden of deeds.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line makes it a promise to anyone that they will stop replaying, and drops 'done with what needed doing', which is the condition. Corrected: 'At ease however things stand, having done what was his to do, the free one is even everywhere; free of craving, he does not dwell on what he did or left undone.'

claim: Wonderful am I, I bow to myself: I own nothing at all, or else all that speech and mind can reach is mine.

heals.why: owning nothing and owning everything come to the same

cultivates.why: aho, wonder
nothing lacking
the self as the all

needs: the wonder is at the self, not the ego; may read as self-praise without that

commentary.reading: Janaka's exclamation after awakening: the self owns nothing as an individual, yet is everything as consciousness.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Knowing the self as one and indestructible, how can you, wise and steady, still delight in piling up wealth?

heals.why: delight in accumulation is questioned

cultivates.why: the indestructible self needs nothing

needs: the listener claims self-knowledge; Ashtavakra is testing Janaka

commentary.reading: Chapter 3 opens the test of Janaka's claimed knowledge: interest in wealth contradicts it.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: Served for money_stress the line tells someone struggling to pay bills not to chase money. Keep for greed or seeker readers only; corrected: 'You know the self as one and indestructible. Wise and steady as you are, how can you still delight in piling up wealth?'

claim: Seeing this world as mere illusion and losing all fascination with it, how could a steady mind fear even death close at hand?

heals.why: fear of death answered by seeing the world as maya

cultivates.why: no fear even at death
vigata-kautuka, fascination gone

needs: only for a seeker who already holds the world to be maya

commentary.reading: Part of the test of Janaka: one who sees the world as mere maya cannot tremble at death.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: None can compare with the great soul whose mind wants nothing even when hope is gone, content in knowing the self.

heals.why: nairashya, hope gone, need not mean collapse
nihspriha, wanting nothing

cultivates.why: atma-jnana-tripta, content in self-knowledge

needs: a portrait of attainment, not a verdict on someone whose plans just failed

commentary.reading: Part of the test of Janaka: one content in the self is unmoved even in nairashya, the absence of all hope.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line turns a portrait of the realised into a promise to anyone whose hopes collapsed. Corrected: 'Who can compare with the great soul whose mind wants nothing even when every hope is gone, content in knowing the Self?'

claim: For one with inner stains dropped, beyond opposites and wishes, pleasure that comes by chance brings neither pain nor elation.

heals.why: nirashih, without wishes

cultivates.why: nirdvandva, neither pain nor elation

commentary.reading: Yadrichchha-labha: the jnani takes what comes unsought without being moved.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

claim: Same in pain and pleasure, full, even in hope and despair, even in life and death: in this way, dissolve now.

heals.why: hope and despair weighed alike

cultivates.why: sama in every pair, including life and death

needs: a seeker practising the dissolution of the separate self

commentary.reading: The fourth of four ways to laya, dissolution of the individual sense: evenness in every pair, up to life and death.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line drops life and death and the instruction to dissolve, and adds 'that evenness is freedom'. Corrected: 'Be the same in pain and pleasure, full in yourself, even in hope and despair, even in life and death. Like this, dissolve now.'

claim: When there is no 'I' there is freedom, and when there is 'I' there is bondage; knowing this, lightly grasp nothing and reject nothing.

heals.why: the I-sense itself is named as bondage

cultivates.why: neither grasping nor rejecting
helaya, lightly

commentary.reading: Aham here is the ego-notion; its absence is moksha. Helaya, playfully or effortlessly.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line adds 'mine' and 'take over', softening the claim that any 'I' is bondage. Corrected: 'When there is no I, there is freedom. When there is I, there is bondage. Knowing this, lightly, grasp nothing and push nothing away.'

claim: Seeing how the great sages, saints and yogis all hold different views, who would not grow weary of it and become calm?

heals.why: the clash of views stops being a reason for agitation
confusion from many doctrines

cultivates.why: shamyati, becomes calm
nirveda toward opinion

needs: the reader is tired of conflicting teachings; it does not say all views are false

commentary.reading: The diversity of doctrines produces nirveda, which turns the seeker from opinion to the self.
commentary.source: Advaita plain sense of the verse; no commentary text opened

line_issue: The line shifts the point from weariness with opinions to quarrelling. Corrected: 'Seeing how differently the great sages, saints and yogis think, who would not tire of opinions and grow quiet?'

claim: Mind, why do you run about confused like a ghost? See the self as undivided, drop attachment, and be happy.

heals.why: the running mind is addressed and stopped
raga-tyaga, dropping attachment

cultivates.why: abhinna, the undivided self

commentary.reading: Dattatreya speaks to his own mind; addressing the mind as other is itself the first step out of it.
commentary.source: Hindi translation in raw_json/avadhuta_gita_source.json; no Sanskrit commentary opened

claim: Free of attachment and aversion, devoted to the good of all beings, firm in understanding and steady, one reaches the highest state.

heals.why: free of aversion

cultivates.why: sarva-bhuta-hite ratah, delighting in the good of all
dhira, steady

commentary.reading: Sarva-bhuta-hite ratah echoes Gita 5.25 and 12.4; service and steadiness are named alongside freedom from raga-dvesha.
commentary.source: Hindi translation in raw_json/avadhuta_gita_source.json; no Sanskrit commentary opened; Gita parallel recalled

line_issue: The line turns 'aversion' into 'grudges' and makes it a command. Corrected: 'One free of attachment and aversion, glad in the good of all beings, firm in understanding and steady, reaches the highest state.'

claim: Thoughts rise and dissolve like bubbles in water; what is there for me to do about them?

heals.why: thoughts are seen as bubbles that pass on their own
no need to fight each thought

cultivates.why: letting the bubbles burst

commentary.reading: Vrittis arise and subside of themselves; the self has nothing to do about them. The first half (pramada, no doubt) is obscure.
commentary.source: Hindi translation in raw_json/avadhuta_gita_source.json; no Sanskrit commentary opened

claim: Why weep, friend? You have no old age, death or birth-sorrow, and no change; I am the nectar of knowledge, sky-like.

heals.why: weeping is questioned from the standpoint of the deathless self

cultivates.why: the self as unchanging, sky-like

needs: only for a seeker for whom the deathless self is already the frame; to a griever it reads as 'stop crying'

commentary.reading: The refrain kim nama rodishi sakhe runs through chapter 3: weeping belongs to one who takes himself as the body.
commentary.source: Hindi translation in raw_json/avadhuta_gita_source.json; no Sanskrit commentary opened

line_issue: Served for grief_general, 'Why weep, friend?' is a rebuke to a mourner. Keep for seeker readers only; the wording is faithful.

claim: Free of union and separation, of enjoying and refusing, the free one walks slowly, slowly, in his natural joy.

heals.why: neither chasing nor refusing

cultivates.why: sahaja-ananda, natural joy
manda manda, unhurried

commentary.reading: Hindi translation: the knower, free of yoga and vairagya, moves slowly in his own natural bliss. 'Imagined by the mind' (manasa kalpita) is read differently by translators.
commentary.source: Hindi translation in raw_json/avadhuta_gita_source.json; no Sanskrit commentary opened

claim: The sage is unshaken by desires, restrained, gentle, pure, owning and seeking nothing, moderate, calm, steady, and has taken refuge in Me.

heals.why: kamair ahata-dhih, mind unharmed by desires

cultivates.why: shanta
mac-charana, refuge in Me
sthira, steady

commentary.reading: The same verse is Bhagavata Purana 11.11.30 (recalled, not verified), where Krishna lists the saint's marks; mac-charana means refuge in the Lord.
commentary.source: Hindi translation in raw_json/avadhuta_gita_source.json; no Sanskrit commentary opened; Bhagavata parallel recalled

line_issue: The line drops 'taken refuge in Me', 'owns nothing' and 'seeks nothing', and adds 'quiet strength'. Corrected: 'Unshaken by desire, restrained, gentle and pure, owning nothing and seeking nothing, moderate in food, calm and steady, the sage takes refuge in Me.'

claim: The sage is compassionate, harms no one, bears with all beings, is true to the core, blameless, even and helpful to all.

heals.why: akrita-droha, harming no one

cultivates.why: kripalu
titikshu, forbearing toward all
sarvopakaraka, helpful to all

commentary.reading: Parallel to Bhagavata 11.11.29 (recalled, not verified): marks of the sadhu. Titiksha is a quality of the saint, not a demand on someone being harmed.
commentary.source: Hindi translation in raw_json/avadhuta_gita_source.json; no Sanskrit commentary opened; Bhagavata parallel recalled

claim: The syllable a marks one freed from the noose of expectation, pure from beginning to end, always abiding in joy.

heals.why: asha-pasha, the noose of hope, is cut
expectation gone

cultivates.why: ever in joy

commentary.reading: First of the four syllables of avadhuta explained as marks of the free person.
commentary.source: Hindi translation in raw_json/avadhuta_gita_source.json; no Sanskrit commentary opened

claim: If another wounds him hard with arrows of harsh words he should stay calm; one cheerful under provocation takes the provoker's merit.

heals.why: the urge to answer harsh words in kind

cultivates.why: staying calm under verbal attack
shama, calm

needs: the reader wants to master their own reaction; not a counsel to tolerate ongoing abuse

commentary.reading: Gita Press: even if badly hurt by arrows of bitter words one should stay calm; one who stays pleased when another rages takes that person's merit.
commentary.source: Gita Press Hindi translation in raw_json/hans_gita_source.json checked; Nilakantha not opened

line_issue: 'Walks away the richer' blurs the verse's claim that the calm one takes the provoker's merit. Corrected: 'If someone pierces you hard with arrows of harsh words, stay calm. The one who stays cheerful when provoked takes the provoker's merit.'

claim: One who restrains the blazing anger an insult stirs, staying clean-hearted, cheerful and free of envy, takes the merit of others.

heals.why: jvalita manyu, blazing anger, is restrained
the sting of the slight is held without poisoning the heart

cultivates.why: restraint under insult
mudita, cheerful

commentary.reading: Restraining the anger born of insult while keeping the heart unspoiled is praised; framed as gain of merit.
commentary.source: Gita Press Hindi translation in raw_json/hans_gita_source.json checked; Nilakantha not opened

claim: One who, spoken to harshly, answers neither harshly nor sweetly, and struck, does not strike back or wish harm: the gods long for him.

heals.why: no harsh reply
no wish for the attacker's harm

cultivates.why: forbearance under blows
dhairya is named as the reason

needs: never as counsel to someone being hit or harmed; a portrait of the forbearing sage

commentary.reading: Gita Press: one who neither strikes back nor wishes ill to the one who struck him, through dhairya, is sought by the gods themselves.
commentary.source: Gita Press Hindi translation in raw_json/hans_gita_source.json checked; Nilakantha not opened

line_issue: Tagged for forgive and betrayal, the line can tell someone being hurt to stay put. Keep descriptive: 'One who answers harsh words neither harshly nor with flattery, and when struck neither strikes back nor wishes harm, is someone the gods long to meet.'

claim: The wise should not answer the ignorant with abuse and insult, for that inflames the other and harms oneself.

heals.why: answering insult with insult is named as self-harm

cultivates.why: seeing the cost to oneself
not feeding the fire

commentary.reading: A rule of speech: returning abuse feeds the other's anger and injures oneself. It governs one's reply, not whether to accept mistreatment.
commentary.source: Gita Press Hindi translation in raw_json/hans_gita_source.json checked; Nilakantha not opened

claim: Going among humans and gods I tell them all: truth is the ladder to heaven, as a boat is the way across the sea.

cultivates.why: truth as the footing of integrity
a clear assurance about where truth leads

commentary.reading: The swan's summary: satya is the single means across.
commentary.source: Gita Press Hindi translation in raw_json/hans_gita_source.json checked; Nilakantha not opened

claim: Among the learned only the wise one is truly happy, stays quiet among many, is strong though weak, and joins no quarrel.

heals.why: staying out of quarrels
strong though weak

cultivates.why: quiet among many
strength not dependent on power

commentary.reading: Gita Press: among brahmanas only the jnani enjoys supreme happiness, stays silent among many, is strong though weak, and quarrels with no one.
commentary.source: Gita Press Hindi translation in raw_json/hans_gita_source.json checked; Nilakantha not opened

claim: Seekers of immortality, this is the work: austerity, restraint, truth, guarding the self, untying the heart's knots, mastering likes and dislikes.

heals.why: dislikes brought under one's own control
likes likewise

cultivates.why: self-restraint and guarding oneself
a clear program of practice

commentary.reading: Gita Press: tapas, dama, satya and mano-nigraha are the best work; untie the knots of the heart and do not rejoice or grieve over pleasant and unpleasant.
commentary.source: Gita Press Hindi translation in raw_json/hans_gita_source.json checked; Nilakantha not opened

claim: Through faith, the teacher's grace and the words 'You are That', a pure mind knows the self and individual as one and stands firm as Meru.

heals.why: the promise is of being unshakable like Meru

cultivates.why: faith in the teacher's word
oneness of atman and jiva
aprakampana, unshaken

needs: accepts the mahavakya teaching

commentary.reading: The standard Advaita path: shraddha, guru-prasada and the mahavakya tat tvam asi yield knowledge of identity, and with it steadiness.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened

line_issue: The line drops 'You are That' and the oneness of the self and the individual, which is the whole content. Corrected: 'With faith, through the teacher's grace and the words You are That, a pure mind comes to know the self and the individual as one, and stands as firm as Mount Meru.'

claim: Having negated everything with 'not this' and tasted awareness in the heart, give up the whole world, as one drinks the water and drops the coconut.

cultivates.why: abandoning the world once its essence is taken
chidghana, dense awareness, tasted in the heart

needs: a renunciate seeker; it is about the world after neti neti, not about a life stage

commentary.reading: Neti neti removes all superimposition; having tasted the self, the world is discarded like the emptied shell.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened

line_issue: Tagged for empty nest and retirement, the line becomes advice about a life stage. The verse prescribes giving up the whole world after negating it. Corrected: 'Having set everything aside with not this, not this, and tasted the nectar of awareness in the heart, let the whole world go, as one drinks the water and sets down the coconut.'

claim: The self is never born and never dies, neither wanes nor grows; ancient, incomparable, blissful, self-luminous, all-pervading, one without a second.

heals.why: the self is beyond birth and death
the self does not perish

cultivates.why: a full description of the self

commentary.reading: Restates Gita 2.20 and Katha 1.2.18: the self is unborn, undying, changeless, non-dual.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened; Gita and Katha parallels recalled

claim: Superimposition is taking one thing for another through error, like a snake seen in a rope; so the world is seen in the Lord.

heals.why: names the mechanism of misperception

cultivates.why: the rope is seen as rope

needs: the reader is a seeker studying Vedanta; for an anxious reader with a real threat it says the threat is imagined

commentary.reading: Definition of adhyasa as in Shankara's adhyasa-bhashya; the world is superimposed on Ishvara as a snake on a rope.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened

line_issue: 'Look again' turns a definition of how the world is superimposed on the Lord into advice for an anxious mind, and drops the Lord. Corrected: 'When through error one thing is taken for another, the wise call it superimposition: a snake seen in a rope. So the world is seen in the Lord.'

claim: Desire, attachment and pleasure belong to the mind and cause bondage; in deep sleep they are absent and the self is felt as happiness.

heals.why: wanting is shown to belong to the mind
the self is happy without it

cultivates.why: the self known as sukha-svarupa from deep sleep

commentary.reading: The sushupti argument: the bliss of dreamless sleep shows happiness is the self's nature, not a product of objects. Self-level with no death or unreality claim.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened

claim: Sitting in a quiet place, senses withdrawn, self-mastered and pure within, contemplate the One with undivided attention, resting in the self.

heals.why: the senses rest and attention gathers

cultivates.why: quiet sitting
the object of contemplation is the self

commentary.reading: Nididhyasana instructions: seclusion, withdrawn senses, single-pointed contemplation of the one self.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened

line_issue: 'Give your full attention to one thing' drops that the object is the One, the self. Corrected: 'Sit somewhere quiet, let the senses rest, master yourself and, pure within, give undivided attention to the One, resting in the self.'

claim: Ever absorbed in the supreme self, content in his own joy and forgetting all else, the free one rests like an ocean of still water.

cultivates.why: svananda, his own joy
tushta, content
like a still ocean

commentary.reading: Portrait of the jivanmukta: content in self-bliss, like a waveless ocean.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened

claim: Until one sees everything as Me, one should be intent on worshipping Me; to one of faith and strong devotion I am visible in the heart always.

heals.why: devotion is given as the way until seeing is complete

cultivates.why: aradhana, worship
shraddhalu, the faithful

commentary.reading: Rama joins bhakti to jnana: worship continues until all is seen as the Lord; the devotee sees him in the heart day and night.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened

line_issue: 'The divine' and 'it' replace Rama speaking as I. Corrected: 'Until you see everything as Me, give yourself to worshipping Me. To one with faith and strong devotion I am visible in the heart, day and night.'

claim: When one has tasted pleasure and pain until weary of them, discernment leads him to freedom from craving.

depicts.why: having tasted enough pleasure and pain to tire of both

cultivates.why: sva-viveka leads
nishkamatva, freedom from craving

commentary.reading: Nirveda is presented as the threshold of wisdom, the classic Vedanta view (cf. Mundaka 1.2.12).
commentary.source: plain sense; no commentary exists that I know of for this text and none was opened; Mundaka parallel recalled

claim: Honour fears disgrace, virtue fears the wicked, power fears critics, and learning fears rival debaters.

depicts.why: the fear that sits inside every achievement

heals.why: every possession of status carries its fear

cultivates.why: seeing the cost of each gain

commentary.reading: Same pattern as Bhartrihari Vairagya Shataka 31 (bhoge roga-bhayam): every worldly good carries its fear. The verse lists, it does not conclude.
commentary.source: plain sense; no commentary exists that I know of for this text and none was opened; Bhartrihari parallel recalled

line_issue: 'Every gain brings a fear' is a fair gloss but is added. Corrected: 'In honour lies the fear of being brought low, in virtue the fear of the wicked, in power the fear of critics, in learning the fear of rival debaters.'

claim: Let go of the world and let go of renouncing it too; renouncing and not renouncing are poison, your nature is pure natural nectar.

heals.why: even renunciation as an achievement is dropped

cultivates.why: freedom from both holding and renouncing
sahaja, the natural state

commentary.reading: The closing verse of chapter 3: both tyaga and atyaga are poison; the self is the natural, pure nectar beyond the pair.
commentary.source: Hindi translation in raw_json/avadhuta_gita_source.json; no Sanskrit commentary opened

line_issue: 'Pride in letting go' invents a point the verse does not make; it says renouncing and not renouncing are both poison. Corrected: 'Let go, let go of the world, and let go of renouncing it too. Renouncing and not renouncing are both poison; your nature is pure, natural nectar.'

claim: Better than punishment is the effort, made with the wise, by which people never come to deserve punishment at all.

heals.why: the urge to punish turns into prevention

cultivates.why: guiding rather than punishing
effort for others' good

commentary.reading: Shiva to the pitris: shaping people so they never need danda is the higher work, done in the company of the wise.
commentary.source: plain sense; no commentary exists that I know of for this text and none was opened

claim: Great suffering comes to the one with a busy mind; how can it touch one beyond the mind? The mind makes the painful resolves.

heals.why: suffering is traced to the mind's own sankalpas

cultivates.why: beyond the mind, no suffering

commentary.reading: Amanaska, the state beyond the mind, is the jivanmukta's; sankalpas are the source of pain.
commentary.source: plain sense; no commentary exists that I know of for this text and none was opened

line_issue: 'Much of our pain' softens 'great suffering comes to the one with a mind'. Corrected: 'Great suffering comes to the one caught in the mind; how could it reach one beyond the mind? It is the mind that makes the resolves that bring pain.'

claim: I take refuge at your feet, Lord, which free from the world; teach me so I may cross the endless ocean of ignorance easily.

depicts.why: Lakshmana asks to be taught how to cross
the ocean of ignorance he feels himself in

cultivates.why: prapanna, taking refuge

commentary.reading: Lakshmana's request opens the Rama Gita; it is the model of the qualified seeker's approach to the teacher.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened

claim: Whoever serves me in the heart, now and then, as beyond or with qualities, becomes me and purifies the three worlds like the sun.

heals.why: even occasional devotion is enough

cultivates.why: seva in the heart
the promise rewards even intermittent turning

commentary.reading: Rama's closing promise: worship of nirguna or saguna, even occasional, leads to identity with him; such a one sanctifies the worlds.
commentary.source: Adhyatma Ramayana Uttara Kanda 5 (Rama Gita), Advaita plain sense; no commentary opened

line_issue: The line drops 'becomes me' and the purifying of the worlds. Corrected: 'Whoever serves me in the heart, even now and then, as beyond qualities or with them, becomes me, and like the sun purifies the three worlds with the dust of his feet.'

claim: By your being alone we exist and are yours, Lord; though we depend on you, we fools forget you through maya.

depicts.why: depending on God and still forgetting
the gods call themselves fools for forgetting

cultivates.why: we exist by your being
ashrita, depending on you

commentary.reading: The gods' confession in their hymn: dependence on the Lord and forgetting through maya.
commentary.source: plain sense; no commentary exists that I know of for this text and none was opened

claim: When the distressed, the seeking and the wanting take refuge in me, my nature becomes a mother, fulfils them, and draws them forward.

heals.why: the distressed are met like a mother meets a child
the one who takes refuge is not alone
needs are met before they are moved on

cultivates.why: assurance of a mother's response
taking refuge

commentary.reading: Echoes the Gita's four kinds of devotees (7.16, arta, jijnasu, artharthi): the Lord's prakriti takes the mother's role toward each.
commentary.source: plain sense; no commentary exists that I know of for this text and none was opened; Gita 7.16 parallel recalled

line_issue: The line drops that she gives them what they long for and then moves them on. Corrected: 'When the hurting, the seeking and the wanting take refuge in me, my nature becomes a mother to them: she gives them what they long for and leads them on toward me.'

claim: Dweller in devotees' hearts, all-pervading one, we come to you alone for refuge; Shambhu, do now whatever will quickly bring us good.

heals.why: the outcome is handed over
no longer deciding what to ask for

cultivates.why: ekantatas, refuge in you alone
trusting the Lord to know the good

commentary.reading: The close of the pitris' hymn: they stop specifying and ask Shiva to do what is good. A prayer the reader can say.
commentary.source: plain sense; no commentary exists that I know of for this text and none was opened

claim: Shiva offers an easy, excellent means by which, even in the hardest work, one never turns away from devotion to him.

heals.why: devotion is kept even inside the hardest work

cultivates.why: never turning from bhakti

needs: the means itself is given in the verses that follow

commentary.reading: Shiva announces the sugama upaya for those whose duties are heavy; this verse is the announcement, not the method.
commentary.source: plain sense; no traditional commentary on this text known to me and none opened

line_issue: The line reads as complete, but the verse only announces the easy way; serve it with the next verse. Corrected: 'Listen, I will tell you an easy way. Holding to it, even in the hardest work, you will not turn away from devotion to me.'

claim: Among touches worthy of reverence, Shiva says, I am the embrace filled with love, affection, devotion and faith.

heals.why: the loving embrace is named as a place of the divine

cultivates.why: sneha, affection
an embrace full of faith

commentary.reading: A vibhuti list in the manner of Gita chapter 10: Shiva names himself as the best in each class.
commentary.source: plain sense; no traditional commentary on this text known to me and none opened

claim: Self-knowing devotees surely cross the ocean of sorrow; the one God is hidden in all beings, beyond doubt.

heals.why: a promise that sorrow can be crossed
na samshayah, no doubt

cultivates.why: atmavid
the one God in all beings

commentary.reading: Quotes Chandogya 7.1.3 (tarati shokam atmavit) and Shvetashvatara 6.11 (eko devah sarvabhuteshu gudhah), recalled; the Upanishads promise crossing, not suppressing, sorrow.
commentary.source: plain sense; no traditional commentary on this text known to me and none opened; Upanishad sources recalled

claim: Shiva's gentle power, whose form is dharma, protects the world; she is eternal and always works for the world's good.

heals.why: the world is held by a power that works for its good
protection is constant

cultivates.why: trust in a protecting order

commentary.reading: Shiva's sattviki shakti is dharma itself, sustaining the world.
commentary.source: plain sense; no traditional commentary on this text known to me and none opened

line_issue: The line removes the speaker ('my power'), which turns a theistic statement into an impersonal one. Corrected: 'My gentle power, whose form is dharma, protects the world. She is eternal and always works for its good.'

claim: We tried in a rush of feeling to speak of what is beyond words; forgive us, Mother, though even this forgiving is your boundless grace.

depicts.why: words fall short before the Mother

heals.why: a fault is met with grace that forgives

cultivates.why: forgiveness itself is recognised as grace
namamah, we bow

needs: the fault is inadequate praise, not a real wrong done to someone

commentary.reading: A stotra's apology for its own inadequacy, ending in grateful surrender.
commentary.source: plain sense; no traditional commentary on this text known to me and none opened

claim: The Mother's grace has no limit; to devotees who cannot grasp her, she shows herself and gives both freedom and well-being.

heals.why: one need not understand fully to be favoured
grace does not wait on complete knowledge

cultivates.why: boundless grace
devotion without full understanding
